43015400.title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer.
43015400.author: Garassino MC
43015400.abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate-has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)-a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study (n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population (n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59-1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

43013352.title: Targeting DHFR to suppress one-carbon metabolism and enhance radiation sensitivity in patients with NRF2-active head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
43013352.author: Zolkind P
43013352.abstract:
PURPOSE: NRF2 hyperactivity is associated with radiation resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) inhibitors pyrimethamine and its potent analog, WCDD115, as radiosensitizing agents through disruption of one-carbon metabolism.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Preclinical studies used NRF2-competent and deficient HNSCC models, clonogenic assays, transcriptomics, metabolomics, pharmacokinetics/toxicity testing, and syngeneic tumor grafts to assess WCDD115 as a novel radiosensitizing agent. In parallel, we conducted an open-label, single-center, window-of-opportunity early phase I clinical trial (NCT05678348) of previously untreated patients with HPV(-) stage III/IV HNSCC to receive pyrimethamine 50mg prior to surgery. Correlative analysis included mass spectrometry, western blotting, and pathway analysis.
RESULTS: WCDD115 enhanced radiation-induced DNA damage and suppressed one-carbon metabolism and nucleotide biosynthesis. Parallel mouse tumor studies demonstrated that WCDD115 enhanced the efficacy of radiation in NRF2-competent but not NRF2-deficient tumors. In a clinical trial of neoadjuvant pyrimethamine, DHFR protein expression was enriched post-treatment by a mean fold change of 9.91 (95% confidence interval 8.1 to 12.2), consistent with a strong on-target effect. The drug was well tolerated with no drug-related grade 3-5 adverse events or surgical delays.
CONCLUSIONS: NRF2 hyperactivity is associated with enhanced one-carbon metabolism which can be therapeutically targeted with DHFR inhibitors to promote radiation sensitization. In HNSCC patients, pyrimethamine achieves potent DHFR inhibition and a favorable safety profile supporting a future phase 2 trial integrating pyrimethamine with definitive radiation-based therapy for NRF2-active HNSCCs.

43008131.title: Prevalence and Actionability of MTAP Loss in Driver Oncogene-Positive and Oncogene-Negative Lung Cancer.
43008131.author: Sakai T
43008131.abstract:
PURPOSE: MTAP loss co-occurs with actionable genomic alterations in NSCLC and creates vulnerability to protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) inhibition. Estimates of prevalence of MTAP loss rely on next-generation sequencing which can underestimate copy losses. Moreover, the activity of PRMT5 inhibitors in oncogene-driven NSCLC is not well established.
EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: We assessed MTAP expression by immunohistochemistry (IHC) in 243 NSCLCs (n=132 early stage, n=111 metastatic), including 33 specimens with paired lymph nodes. Activity of PRMT5 inhibitor monotherapy and in combination with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) was evaluated in MTAP-deleted NSCLC cell lines harboring EGFR or KRAS mutations or ALK rearrangements.
RESULTS: Among 243 NSCLC specimens from 240 patients (72% with driver alterations, 90% adenocarcinoma), MTAP loss was identified in 42 (17%) specimens, including 17 (13%) early-stage and 22 (20%) metastatic specimens. MTAP loss occurred in 24% of stage 4 driver-positive NSCLCs versus 14% of driver-negative tumors (p=0.314). Twenty-one (64%) lung-nodal pairs demonstrated concordance; eight cases only exhibited decreased MTAP expression in nodes. Variable sensitivity to PRMT5 inhibitors was observed in 22 MTAP-deleted NSCLC cell lines (9 EGFR-mutant, 7 KRAS-mutant, 6 ALK-rearranged), with responses seen in TKI-sensitive and TKI-resistant lines. SDMA (symmetric dimethylarginine) expression did not predict PRMT5 inhibitor sensitivity. TKI + PRMT5 inhibitor combos had greater activity than monotherapy.
CONCLUSIONS: MTAP loss occurs in 17% of NSCLC, including 24% of oncogene-driven tumors. PRMT5 inhibitor activity is independent of TKI exposure and SDMA expression and enhanced by TKI therapy. These findings support evaluation of PRMT5 inhibitor + TKIs in oncogene-driven NSCLC.

43002516.title: BRCA1 at the Crossroads of Genome Stability, Mitochondrial Homeostasis, and Tumor Immunity.
43002516.author: Gohari Z
43002516.abstract: BRCA1 has long been recognized as a guardian of genome integrity through its essential role in homologous recombination (HR)-mediated DNA repair. While HR deficiency underlies the clinical efficacy of Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors (PARPi), therapeutic responses remain incomplete, highlighting the need to identify vulnerabilities beyond defective DNA repair. Recent evidence has expanded the biological landscape of BRCA1, revealing critical roles in mitochondrial (mt) quality control, metabolic homeostasis, redox regulation, and innate immune signaling. Together, these functions support an integrated genome-mitochondria-immune axis through which BRCA1 coordinates cellular adaptation to stress. Disruption of this network amplifies genomic instability, promotes metabolic rewiring and inflammatory signaling, and generates vulnerabilities extending beyond HR deficiency. Mitochondrial dysfunction resulting from BRCA1 loss reinforces tumor progression through mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) instability, oxidative stress, and tumor microenvironment remodeling while creating opportunities for therapeutic intervention. Viewing BRCA1 deficiency through this integrated framework broadens the concept of synthetic lethality and provides a rationale for combination strategies integrating PARP inhibition with mitochondrial-targeted agents, metabolic therapies, epigenetic modulators, and immune-based approaches. This perspective positions BRCA1 as a central regulator of nuclear-mitochondrial crosstalk and highlights emerging opportunities to overcome therapeutic resistance and advance precision oncology.

43002139.title: Kinetics of Re-differentiation with Short-Course Dabrafenib and Trametinib in Patients with Radioiodine-Refractory Thyroid Cancer.
43002139.author: Yang SP
43002139.abstract:
PURPOSE: MAPK pathway activation suppresses iodine-handling genes, including sodium-iodide symporter (NIS), contributing to loss of iodine avidity in radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancer. Prior BRAF/ MEK inhibitor re-differentiation trials improved iodine uptake but used empiric 4-6 week treatment. The timing of maximal NIS re-expression remains undefined. We evaluated whether short course dabrafenib plus trametinib restores iodine uptake and provides clinical benefit.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this multicentre phase II trial, patients with progressive metastatic radioiodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma harbouring BRAFV600E or RAS mutations received dabrafenib and trametinib. I-124 PET/CT dosimetry was performed at baseline and after 2 weeks, with repeat imaging at week 4 post therapy if dosimetry criteria was not met. Radioiodine was administered once criteria was met. The primary endpoint was attainment of predicted lesional absorbed dose ≥20 Gy with I-131 activity ≤300 mCi. Secondary endpoints included RECIST response, progression-free survival (PFS), thyroglobulin response, and safety.
RESULTS: Nine of 14 patients (64%) met the dosimetry criteria and received radioiodine; 6 out of 9 (67%) restored iodine uptake within 2 weeks. Among radioiodine-treated patients, best objective response rate within 6 months was 75% by RECIST. Median PFS was 10.8 months. RAS-mutant tumours demonstrated greater lesion regression than BRAFV600E-mutant tumours. Early reduction in stimulated thyroglobulin and preserved FOXE1 nuclear localisation, and higher tumour-to-normal GLIS3 nuclear expression were associated with re-differentiation response.
CONCLUSIONS: Short-course dabrafenib/ trametinib can induce rapid re-differentiation within 2 weeks in a subset of patients with MAPK-driven radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancer, supporting individualized BRAF/MEK inhibition duration rather than empiric prolonged treatment.

43025066.title: Factors associated with chemotherapy free interval (CFI) after induction chemotherapy in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) based on a meta-analysis on ARCAD CRC database: The CFI-SCORE project.
43025066.author: Muller M
43025066.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: After induction therapy, maintenance strategies in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remain uncertain. Treatment breaks and a chemotherapy-free interval (CFI) may be considered when tumour control is achieved as well as maintenance therapy. Identifying variables of a short/intermediate/long CFI would be useful to guide therapeutic decisions.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: CFI-SCORE is an individual patient data meta-analysis assessing clinical and biological factors of short (<3 months), intermediate (3-6 months) or long (≥6-12 months) CFI after induction chemotherapy. Data from 6 international trials comparing observation with continued systemic therapy were pooled. An exploratory score was developed using significant variables.
RESULTS: A total of 1188 patients were analysed. Median CFI was 3.67 months; 406 (34.2%), 503 (42.3%), and 279 (23.5%) patients had short, intermediate, and long CFIs, respectively. In multivariable analysis, male sex (adjusted OR [95% CI]: 1.36 [1.04-1.79]), age ≥ 75 years (1.52 [0.99-2.35]), left-sided or rectal primary tumour (1.38 [1.01-1.87]), prior resection of the primary tumour (1.38 [1.06-1.79]), a single metastatic site (1.51 [1.16-1.97]), and absence of thrombocytosis (1.41 [1.00-2.00]) were associated with longer CFI. The exploratory score showed modest discrimination for 6-month CFI prediction (bootstrap-corrected C-statistic, 0.56); the OS C-index was 0.59.
DISCUSSION: CFI-SCORE is the first meta-analysis assessing CFI after induction therapy in mCRC. Six parameters were associated with CFI in patients with responding/stable disease and were combined into an exploratory score and nomogram. These results are hypothesis-generating: prospective validation is needed to determine whether CFI-SCORE could guide treatment-break vs maintenance strategies.

43018467.title: Perivascular epithelial remodeling is reflected in circulating cfDNA methylation signals as detection markers for early esophageal tumorigenesis.
43018467.author: Yi Y
43018467.abstract: Early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is hindered by a lack of noninvasive biomarkers for precancerous lesions. Here, we report a circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation approach for early esophageal neoplasia detection. In prospective community screening, the assay achieved standardized sensitivity of 78% at 79% specificity for the clinically actionable endpoint of high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (HGIN) or ESCC, with stage-specific sensitivities of 76% for HGIN and 86% for ESCC. Genome-wide methylation profiling reveals HGIN as an early epigenetic reprogramming stage. Integrative spatial and single-cell RNA sequencing reveals pronounced remodeling of the endothelial-proximal epithelial cell population, whose methylation signatures are detected in cfDNA. Guided by these findings, we develop an 11-gene cfDNA methylation panel that shows robust discrimination of early-stage ESCC across three retrospective case-control sets and an independent screening-derived case-control set. Together, these results demonstrate that our cfDNA methylation panel has promising utility for early ESCC detection.

43014141.title: Liver cancer incidence trends in younger versus older adults over time: an analysis of population-based cancer registry data.
43014141.author: Rumgay H
43014141.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver cancer epidemiology is evolving, yet age-specific patterns remain poorly characterized. We aimed to assess variation in age-specific liver cancer incidence trends based on population-based cancer registry data.
METHODS: We extracted annual liver cancer incidence (1978-2017) for 47 countries from Cancer Incidence in Five Continents Plus. Age-standardized incidence rates (ASRs) were compared over time and over the most recent decade for three age-groups (15-49, 50-69, 70 +) using Estimated Annual Percentage Change (EAPC) in 38 populations.
FINDINGS: From 1978-2017, ASRs declined in high-incidence countries in Eastern and South-Eastern Asia but increased in low-incidence countries across Northern America, Australia/New Zealand, and Northern Europe. During 2008-2017, ASRs among younger adults (15-49) declined in 11 of 38 male populations (EAPC -10.0% in France) and in females in the Republic of Korea (-3.7%) and China (-2.6%). In older adults (50-69 and 70 +), ASRs declined in high-incidence countries (Republic of Korea, Japan, China) during 2008-2017, while increasing in 15 male populations and 11 female populations (age 50-69) and in 12 male populations and 10 female populations (age 70 +), mostly in Northern and Western Europe and Northern America. Overall, trends in hepatocellular carcinoma and cholangiocarcinoma were heterogeneous across countries, with interpretation limited by substantial variation in histologically unspecified cases.
INTERPRETATION: Rising liver cancer rates among older adults in historically low-incidence countries might suggest a shift from infectious to noncommunicable causes. In contrast, declines in younger adults in historically high-incidence countries may signal the positive impact of hepatitis and aflatoxin control. Strengthened, targeted prevention remains essential to prevent liver cancer globally.

43003077.title: A stroma-sensing TGF-β blockade reprograms CAF-myeloid niches to induce durable tumor immunity.
43003077.author: Kang DW
43003077.abstract: Transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) accumulation in the tumor microenvironment (TME) is a major barrier to durable antitumor immunity. We developed fibronectin extra domain B (FN-EDB)-binding peptide (FEBP)-soluble TβRII-Fc (sTβRII), an engineered inhibitor targeting the FN-EDB-rich tumor matrix for localized TGF-β blockade. In fibrotic, immune-excluded tumors, FEBP-sTβRII suppresses TGF-β/SMAD signaling to unleash T cell activation and IFN-γ production, thereby driving feedforward cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-myeloid reprogramming toward an antigen-presenting state. This coordinated remodeling relieves immune exclusion and converts the fibrotic TME into an antigen-visible ecosystem that sustains robust T cell infiltration and activation. Consequently, FEBP-sTβRII induces T cell-dependent tumor regression, expands effector-memory populations, and elicits long-term, cross-protective antitumor immunity, while minimizing peripheral transcriptional disturbances compared with systemic sTβRII. Together, these findings show that spatially targeted TGF-β blockade overcomes fibrotic immune exclusion to establish durable local and systemic tumor immunity.

43024837.title: When Safety Depends on Coincidence: A Near-Miss in Radium-223 Therapy Revealing Latent Vulnerabilities in Theranostics Emergency Care.
43024837.author: Makino S
43024837.abstract: This article presents a near-miss event in which a patient with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer underwent emergency orthopedic surgery 21 days after Radium-223 administration. A safe outcome in this case depended on two coincidences: an incidental discovery of treatment history by a nurse and sufficient elapsed time for decay and clearance. Without the former, surgery would have proceeded without radiological assessment or appropriate precautions; without the latter, standard radiation safety precautions alone would have been insufficient to manage the hazard even with full radiological awareness. Through root cause analysis, we identified an information gap and an unrecognized dependence on favorable boundary conditions as the primary latent vulnerabilities. To quantify the unmanaged hazard, a deterministic hazard estimation demonstrated that surface contamination could have reached 386-fold above the US regulatory limit if the emergency had occurred 1 hour after administration. However, it fell sharply to approximately the regulatory limit at 24 hours due to physical decay and biological clearance. Crucially, even with minimal hemorrhage (30 mL), the contamination 1 hour after administration would still exceed the US statutory threshold 5.8-fold. These findings support a conceptual reframing: time functions as an intrinsic safety measure in radioisotope therapy by reducing the hazard itself through physical decay and biological clearance, independent of human compliance. Because compliance-driven administrative controls remain vulnerable during acute emergencies, institutions must explicitly operationalize time as an autonomous safety measure. To achieve this, we propose a three-tiered governance framework established at therapy initiation-that explicitly recognizes time as an intrinsic safety measure-assigning clear responsibilities to the prescribing physician as the primary clinical lead, the Radiation Safety Committee for operational protocols, and hospital executive management for infrastructure deployment.

43009643.title: A novel candidate biomarker for detecting premalignant and early ovarian cancer.
43009643.author: Monson KR

43009642.title: Blood-based RNA biomarker for the early detection of ovarian cancer.
43009642.author: Wilhelm J
43009642.abstract: Flower-Win/Lose signaling underlies a tumor-host fitness conflict in ovarian cancer, in which tumor-derived exosomal Tu-stroma reduces the fitness of surrounding host cells, favoring tumor expansion within host tissues. High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), the most prevalent histotype of epithelial ovarian cancer and leading cause of ovarian-cancer-related mortality, arises from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), a noninvasive precursor typically identifiable only by histopathologic examination of excised fallopian tube tissue. Here we evaluated Tu-stroma, a tumor-associated long noncoding RNA enriched in serum extracellular vesicles (EVs), as a circulating biomarker in STIC and early-stage HGSC, representing the earliest histopathologically defined phases of disease. Tu-stroma was quantified in serum EVs from 506 individuals with histologically normal adnexa, benign-adnexal lesions, isolated STIC and HGSC across International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stages I-IV. Normalized EV Tu-stroma ΔCT values were elevated in STIC (n = 43) and HGSC (n = 232) versus controls (n = 143) and benign-adnexal lesions (n = 88), including premenopausal women (controls = 57, benign = 34, STIC = 32, HGSC = 88). In paired receiver operating characteristic analyses, Tu-stroma showed higher discrimination than cancer antigen 125 (CA125) for STIC versus controls (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.99 versus 0.59, P < 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.99 versus 0.31, P < 0.001), and for HGSC versus controls (AUC = 0.99 versus 0.96, P = 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.98 versus 0.84, P < 0.001). Tu-stroma showed no systematic elevation across inflammatory or physiologic comparators (n = 116) or nonovarian malignancies (n = 160), each assessed against healthy controls (n = 100), supporting disease-context specificity. Modeled risk-enriched contexts yielded predictive values compatible with intended-use populations. These findings identify Tu-stroma as a candidate EV-RNA marker associated with pre-invasive and early HGSC biology. Prospective evaluation in consecutively enrolled real-world cohorts is required to validate diagnostic performance, predictive value and clinical utility.

43008753.title: Risovalisib for PIK3CA-mutated recurrent or persistent ovarian clear cell carcinoma: a single-arm, multicentre, phase 2 trial.
43008753.author: Li J
43008753.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma is a rare but aggressive and biologically distinct subtype of ovarian cancer, in which PIK3CA mutations are common. Advanced ovarian clear cell carcinoma is very difficult to treat, and after failure of platinum-based chemotherapy, therapeutic options are limited. We aimed to evaluate the anti-tumour activity and safety of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, for treatment of patients with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma.
METHODS: We conducted a single-arm, phase 2 trial of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, in 27 centres in China and 12 centres in Japan. Eligible participants were adult patients (aged 18 years or older, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1) with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma and one to three lines of previous systemic anti-tumour treatment. Risovalisib was given orally at 40 mg daily in 21-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other protocol-defined reasons for discontinuation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate assessed by blinded independent review committee (BIRC) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (version 1.1), among all treated patients with a confirmed PIK3CA hotspot mutation and baseline tumour assessments with measurable lesions per BIRC (efficacy analysis set). The primary endpoint was considered met if the lower 95% CI was greater than 8%. Safety analyses were performed in all patients who received at least one dose of risovalisib (safety analysis set). The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05043922) and is ongoing but no longer recruiting patients.
FINDINGS: Between Oct 6, 2021, and Jan 31, 2024, 93 patients were enrolled and received risovalisib. The median age was 49 years (IQR 43-58), all patients were female, 52 (56%) were from Japan, 41 (44%) were from China, and 63 (68%) had two or more previous lines of therapy. The median duration of follow-up was 14·5 months (IQR 8·6-18·3). The objective response rate was 29 (35% [95% CI 25-46]) of 84 patients in the efficacy analysis set. The most commonly reported grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 93 patients were rash (30 [32%]), hyperglycaemia (28 [30%]), and decreased weight (7 [8%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 36 (39%) patients, the most common being rash (eight [9%]), pneumonitis (six [6%]), and decreased appetite (four [4%]). There were no treatment-related deaths.
INTERPRETATION: These results support risovalisib as a potential novel treatment option for PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma, a rare yet lethal cancer in dire need of additional treatment options. Combination strategies including risovalisib could also be explored to further increase efficacy observed in this study.
FUNDING: Haihe Biopharma.

43020097.title: Empirical tuberculosis treatment in infants living with HIV hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa (EMPIRICAL): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, 2 × 2 factorial, controlled superiority trial.
43020097.author: Domínguez-Rodríguez S
43020097.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high globally. The EMPIRICAL trial evaluated whether empirical tuberculosis treatment (eTB-T) improves survival compared with the currently recommended microbiologically and clinically guided strategy.
METHODS: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2×2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia, without a current tuberculosis diagnosis or contact, were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity. A computer-generated block randomisation schedule was used, with fixed blocks of eight allocations (two allocations to each factorial treatment group) within each stratum. Participants received standard of care (SoC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SoC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. Here, we report the comparison between the eTB-T (ie, SoC plus tuberculosis treatment and SoC plus oral valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and non-eTB-T (ie, SoC or SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir) groups. Nasopharyngeal aspirates, stools for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing, and urine for tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay were collected at recruitment. In the non-eTB-T groups, tuberculosis treatment was initiated if microbiological results collected at recruitment yielded positive results or if, during follow-up, the treating clinician suspected tuberculosis on clinical grounds, including radiological findings, in accordance with routine clinical practice and guidelines. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality (at 15 days and 360 days). Survival was estimated using flexible parametric models with covariate-adjusted conditional estimates; missing data were imputed by chained equations. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03915366) and is now complete.
FINDINGS: Between March 15, 2020, and Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were analysed after excluding five patients who did not meet eligibility criteria. 276 participants were allocated to the eTB-T groups (n=140 eTB-T and n=136 valganciclovir plus eTB-T) and 282 to the non-eTB-T groups (n=142 SoC and n=140 valganciclovir). 17 (6%) of 276 in the eTB-T groups and 20 (7%) of 282 in the non-eTB-T groups were lost to follow-up. Median age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4) and 274 (49%) of participants were female and 284 (51%) were male. In the non-eTB-T groups, 130 (46%) of 282 participants eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment at a median of 4·0 days (IQR 3·0-15·0) after recruitment due to positive microbiological findings in 55 (20%) cases (53 confirmed by tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay and two by nasopharyngeal aspirates Xpert MTB/RIF) or clinical decision in 75 (27%) cases. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and eTB-T (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19, 95% CI 0·73-1·95; pheterogeneity=0·4836). At 12 months, 132 (48%) of 276 participants in eTB-T groups and 121 (43%) of 282 participants in non-eTB-T groups died. In the eTB-T groups, the adjusted hazard ratio for death was 1·12 (95% CI 0·87-1·43; p=0·3868). At 15 days, the odds ratio was 1·24 (95% CI 0·83-1·84; p=0·2950). Serious adverse events did not differ between groups (1·19, 0·82-1·73; p=0·3523). There were no treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events were elevation of transaminases (72 [26%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 74 [26%] in the non-eTB-T group), anaemia (163 [59%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 169 [60%] in the non-eTB-T groups), and infectious disease requiring antimicrobial treatment (161 [58%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 176 [62%] in the non-eTB-T groups).
INTERPRETATION: In contrast to empirical treatment with valganciclovir, there was no evidence that eTB-T was superior to a clinically and microbiologically guided strategy in reducing all-cause mortality among infants with HIV-associated pneumonia. However, the high proportion of infants who eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment during follow-up in the non-eTB-T groups might have reduced the contrast between strategies and attenuated the ability to detect differences in outcomes.

43018988.title: Early vs Routine Oral Nutritional Supplementation During Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
43018988.author: Su L
43018988.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Oral nutritional supplementation (ONS), providing supplementary oral nutrition in addition to usual food, is widely used during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), but its optimal timing and cost utility remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate efficacy and explore cost utility of early ONS in patients with NPC undergoing CCRT.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted at 6 Chinese tertiary hospitals from July 2021 to May 2025. Eligible patients were aged 18 to 70 years with newly diagnosed stage II to IVA NPC, a Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA) score of 0 to 8, and planned CCRT. Key exclusions included oral intake less than 60% of requirements for 3 days or longer, inability or unwillingness to receive concurrent chemotherapy, and inability to receive oral or enteral nutrition. Data were analyzed from November 2025 to March 2026.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomized 1:1 to early ONS at CCRT start or routine ONS after prespecified nutritional decline.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was the incidence of more than 5% weight loss from baseline to CCRT completion. Secondary end points included PG-SGA score, the incidence of grade 3 or higher radiation-induced oral mucositis (RIOM), quality of life (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30), and radiotherapy interruption. Cost utility measures included total cost, utility, and incremental cost utility ratio.
RESULTS: Of 242 patients screened, 236 patients were randomized, and the prespecified modified intention-to-treat population included 216 patients (mean [SD] age, 46.62 [11.19] years; 168 [77.8%] male), with 107 receiving early ONS and 109 receiving routine ONS. More than 5% weight loss occurred in 70 participants (65.4% ) in the early ONS group, compared with 88 participants (80.7%) in the routine ONS group (relative risk [RR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.68-0.96; P = .01). An intention-to-treat analysis including all randomized participants yielded a similar estimate (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.65-0.93). In the modified intention-to-treat population, grade 3 or higher RIOM occurred in 15 participants (14.0%) in the early ONS group vs 29 participants (26.6%) in the routine ONS group (RR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.30-0.93). Best-case costs were $9560.56 in the early ONS group vs $9685.23 in the routine ONS group, with quality-adjusted life-years of 0.1144 vs 0.1132, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that early ONS reduced clinically meaningful weight loss during CCRT; exploratory analyses suggested potential benefits for severe RIOM and a potentially favorable short-term economic profile.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04823468.

43018983.title: Perioperative Camrelizumab Plus Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
43018983.author: Liu F
43018983.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Despite multimodal treatment, recurrence remains common in patients with resectable locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Whether perioperative chemoimmunotherapy improves long-term outcomes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effect of perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy on event-free survival (EFS) compared with standard surgery-based treatment in patients with resectable locally advanced HNSCC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The CAMORAL trial was a multicenter, phase 2 randomized clinical trial conducted at 4 academic hospitals in China between October 2020 and March 2024, with data cutoff on April 11, 2025. Patients aged 18 to 75 years with untreated, resectable stage III to IVB HNSCC were assigned to neoadjuvant-adjuvant treatment or control. Analyses used the intention-to-treat population. Data were analyzed from May 2025 to February 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive two 21-day cycles of neoadjuvant camrelizumab, 200 mg, plus albumin-bound paclitaxel and carboplatin followed by surgery, risk-adapted adjuvant therapy, and maintenance camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles; or upfront surgery followed by standard risk-adapted adjuvant therapy.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was 2-year EFS. Secondary end points included major pathological response (MPR), pathological complete response (pCR), overall survival, 2-year distant metastasis-free survival, 2-year locoregional recurrence-free survival, and safety.
RESULTS: Of 125 included patients, 99 (79.2%) were male, and the mean (SD) age was 56.3 (11.7) years. A total of 63 patients were assigned to the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 62 to the control group; the median (IQR) follow-up was 24.6 (16.8-36.5) months. A total of 103 (82.4%) had oral cavity primary tumors. Among 125 patients, the 2-year EFS rate was 77.8% (95% CI, 63.6-87.0) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group compared with 46.1% (95% CI, 31.3-59.6) in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.17-0.68; P = .001). MPR and pCR were 47.6% (95% CI, 34.9-60.6) and 25.4% (95% CI, 15.3-37.9), respectively, in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group, with no MPR or pCR events in the control group. The 2-year overall survival rates were 92.0% and 69.1%, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.10-0.64); the hazard ratio of 2-year distant metastasis-free survival was 0.15 (95% CI, 0.03-0.68). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 50 of 63 patients (79.4%) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 35 of 62 patients (56.5%) in the control group; 1 fatal treatment-emergent adverse event occurred in the control group.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this phase 2 randomized clinical trial, perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly improved EFS with manageable toxic effects, supporting evaluation of intensified perioperative immune priming in resectable HNSCC.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR.org.cn Identifier: ChiCTR2000037980.

43024850.title: Dasatinib Dose Optimization With Weekend Drug Holiday for Improved Tolerability in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (DasaHIT): A German Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Alliance Randomized Trial.
43024850.author: La Rosée P
43024850.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare standard-dose dasatinib 100 mg once daily with reduced-dose using a weekend drug holiday to improve tolerability for patients with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with chronic phase CML (CP-CML) were randomly assigned to either receive standard-of-care dasatinib 100 mg once daily or an intermittent dasatinib schedule (5 days on, 2 days [weekend] off) in a prospective multicenter phase III trial. Achievement of major molecular remission (MMR) at 24 months and a newly developed cumulative toxicity score were coprimary end points.
RESULTS: Of 289 eligible patients, 147 were assigned to standard-of-care dasatinib and 142 to intermittent dosing. Eighty percent of patients received first-line treatment (n = 232). In the standard arm, 105 of 130 patients (81% [95% CI, 74% to 88%) achieved MMR at 24 months compared with 101 of 130 patients (78% [95% CI, 71% to 85%]) in the experimental arm resulting in noninferiority within the prespecified noninferiority margin of 15% (P = .009). Among second- or later-line patients, MMR at 24 months was 24% lower, failing noninferiority. Comparison of grade 2-4 toxicities revealed no significant difference between the treatment arms. However, a post hoc analysis of toxicities of special interest (pleural effusion/pericardial effusion) showed 21 of 130 patients (16%) in the standard arm versus 10 of 125 (8%) patients in the experimental arm (P = .0464). Consistently, health-related quality of life improved mainly in first-line patients, with more favorable outcomes in the experimental arm.
CONCLUSION: Intermittent dasatinib dosing with weekend treatment holidays in patients with CP-CML is noninferior to continuous dosing with respect to MMR at 24 months, at least in the first-line setting. The incidence of pleural or pericardial effusion appears to be reduced compared with standard-of-care continuous dosing.

43023550.title: Aligning Clinical Trial Reporting: A systematic analysis and position statement by the International Consortium for MDS.
43023550.author: Brunner AM
43023550.abstract: Variability in how clinical trial elements are reported can hinder accurate interpretation and comparison of trial results. Here, we systematically analyzed published manuscripts of therapeutic clinical trials in myelodysplastic syndromes/neoplasms (MDS) focusing on how key data elements were reported and made recommendations on how to improve this reporting. We included peer-reviewed full text manuscripts that reported results of clinical trials in MDS and were published between January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2024. We analyzed the presence or absence of several pre-determined key reporting elements and then synthesized these data to evaluate for consistency across manuscripts. We identified substantial variability in descriptions of patient characteristics, as well as the definitions used for response criteria. For example, baseline ANC was reported in only 16% of lower-risk MDS studies and 23% of higher-risk MDS studies, while baseline bone marrow blast percentage was reported in only 55% of higher-risk MDS manuscripts. In addition, response endpoints lacked standardization, with six unique definitions of RBC transfusion independence identified in lower-risk MDS trials and seven different definitions of overall response rate identified in higher-risk MDS trials. Informed by the results of this analysis, we then performed a modified-Delphi process for members of the International Consortium for MDS (icMDS) to develop consensus-based recommendations for consistent and accurate reporting of MDS clinical trial results. We advocate that these recommendations serve as benchmarks and templates for clinical trial reporting in MDS to improve interpretability and comparison of results.

43023553.title: CAR-T Targeting of Mutant Calreticulin Selectively Eradicates Myeloproliferative Neoplasm-Sustaining Stem Cells.
43023553.author: Choi DC
43023553.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) arise from and are sustained by hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that acquire a driver mutation. Existing therapies fail to eliminate MPN HSCs, leaving allogeneic HSC transplantation (HSCT) as the only curative option. However, allogeneic HSCT non-selectively ablates both healthy and MPN HSCs, requiring donor stem-cell replacement and risking serious toxicities and death. MPN driver mutations in calreticulin (CALRmut) generate a shared C-terminal neopeptide unique to MPN cells that must be displayed at the cell surface in complex with the thrombopoietin receptor MPL to drive oncogenic signaling. These features make CALRmut an attractive target for selective immunotherapy. However, it is unknown whether MPN HSCs consistently display surface CALRmut to enable selective elimination in vivo via CALRmut targeting. We generated hAB2, a high-affinity CALRmut-specific humanized antibody, to use as the binding domain for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. We show that functional murine and human MPN HSCs express surface CALRmut that is reliably detected by AB2 in vitro and in vivo. We developed an MPN patient-derived tumor xenograft (PDTX) model to enable rigorous testing of human MPN HSC-directed therapies in vivo. hAB2 CAR-T cells selectively eliminate CALRmut MPN HSCs in PDTX, eradicating all detectable MPN-propagating function in serial transplantation assays, while preserving co-existing normal human and host hematopoiesis. These findings establish cell-surface CALRmut display as a therapeutically exploitable feature of MPN HSCs and support the feasibility of CALRmut-targeted, transplant-free immunotherapies with curative intent for CALRmut MPNs.

43023552.title: Optimizing Reduced-Intensity Conditioning for Older Patients with AML and MDS: A Large-Scale Analysis from the CIBMTR.
43023552.author: Kongtim P
43023552.abstract: The optimal reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC) regimen for older patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (AHCT) remains undefined. We utilized CIBMTR registry data (2013-2022) to compare five common fludarabine-based regimens in 11,731 patients aged ≥50 years: fludarabine combined with 2 days of busulfan (FB2), melphalan 100 mg/m² (FM100), melphalan 140 mg/m² (FM140), or 2 Gy TBI with (FCT) or without (FT) cyclophosphamide. Using propensity score inverse probability weighting and Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART), we found that Fludarabine-melphalan (FM) regimens demonstrated superior long-term survival. Although FM140, FCT, and FT showed higher early mortality (≤6 months) than FB2 (P=.036), both FM100 (HR 0.79) and FM140 (HR 0.77) achieved significantly better late (> 6 months) overall survival (OS), outperforming all other regimens (P<.0001). In the 2019-2022 cohort, FM100, FM140, and FCT provided improved disease-free survival (DFS) relative to FB2. Specifically, FM100 yielded superior DFS compared to FCT (P=0.002) and FT (P=0.007). FM-based conditioning consistently resulted in lower relapse rates (P<.0001) and improved late GVHD-free/relapse-free survival. While FM regimens faced higher early non-relapse mortality (NRM), this impact did not persist beyond 6 months. BART analysis confirmed that these survival and relapse benefits remained robust across various patient comorbidities. In conclusion, FM100 and FM140 provide superior long-term survival and DFS for older patients with AML/MDS by providing potent anti-leukemic activity that offsets higher early toxicity. These findings support FM-based RIC as the preferred conditioning platform for this population, regardless of baseline comorbidities.

43020918.title: Differentiation hierarchy in adult B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia at clonal resolution.
43020918.author: Geßner A
43020918.abstract: While a differentiation hierarchy with leukemia-initiating stem cells (LICs) at the apex is well documented for acute myeloid leukemia, the existence of LICs and their trajectories in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) are debated. This study aims to investigate the hierarchical landscape of two B-ALL cases by combining barcoding and multiome single-cell data to unveil the differentiation architecture and temporal dynamics of leukemic differentiation at clonal and single-cell resolution in vivo. Single-cell transcriptome and AbSeq analysis of lentiviral barcoded and transplanted patient-derived B-ALL cells revealed interconnected subpopulations, which could be prospectively isolated via surface markers and exhibited distinct leukemogenicity. Barcode tracking demonstrated the ability of cells to differentiate from a source cluster into differentiated progeny. Using machine learning, we identified expression patterns predicting the differentiation potential of each barcoded cell within the immature cell compartment. To determine the dynamical properties of clones, we developed a mathematical model that simulates the development of these subpopulations from a clonally diverse stem cell compartment. The model confirmed the most likely cluster of origin, supporting our functional data, and revealed the variability in dynamical properties between clones, while largely excluding plasticity. Hence, our work demonstrates unidirectional differentiation in selected B-ALL cases.

43020916.title: Genomic and transcriptomic features associated with responses and outcomes of third-generation tyrosine kinase-inhibitor therapy in chronic myeloid leukemia.
43020916.author: Zhang X
43020916.abstract: Third-generation tyrosine-kinase inhibitors (3G-TKIs), including olverembatinib and ponatinib, are effective in people with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) failing prior TKIs, but many subjects still have poor responses and outcomes. The broader genomic and transcriptomic features associated with 3G-TKI prognosis remain incompletely defined. We interrogated genomic and transcriptomic data from 202 subjects receiving olverembatinib or ponatinib at baseline and during therapy. In penalized multi-variable analyses, the high-burden ASXL1 p.G646Wfs*12 (ASXL1G646Wfs*12) variant emerged as the most consistent genomic feature associated with inferior responses and outcomes; additional lower-frequency variants, including RUNX1, IKZF1, PHF6, SETBP1 and GATA2 variants, were also associated with responses and/or outcomes. Longitudinal genomic analyses showed that ABL1 variants frequently decreased during 3G-TKI therapy, whereas persistent, emerging or expanding non-ABL1 variant clones were enriched in resistant subjects, suggesting a shift toward BCR::ABL1-independent clonal evolution in later-line resistance. Transcriptomic analyses identified three distinct gene expression profiles (GEPs) based clusters with different prognoses. Favorable prognosis was associated with lower leukemic stemness and more immune-active transcriptional features, whereas poor prognosis was characterized by stemness- and proliferation-dominant, immune-suppressed states. These findings identify genomic and transcriptomic features associated with 3G-TKI prognosis and provide a potential framework for molecular risk stratification in later-line CML that requires independent validation.

43016394.title: Clonal hematopoiesis in long-term survivors after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation: associations with active chronic graft-versus-host disease, donor age, and transplantation for chronic myeloid leukemia.
43016394.author: Toya T
43016394.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) in long-term survivors of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) remains largely understudied. Using targeted sequencing, we analyzed peripheral blood samples from 101 patients who survived without relapse for more than 10 years after HCT. The median interval from HCT to sample collection was 13.8 years (range, 10.0-29.8 years). Thirty-six CHs with ≥2% variant allele frequency were detected in 29 patients (28.7%). Complete blood count did not differ according to CH status. Multivariable analysis showed donor age at sampling (odds ratio [OR] 1.06, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.00-1.12), patients who underwent HCT for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML; OR 7.13, 95% CI 1.38-36.8), and moderate/severe chronic graft-versushost disease at sampling (OR 5.49, 95% CI 1.05-28.7) were significantly associated with CH. Donor age at sampling was significantly higher in patients with pathogenic CH than in those with variants of unknown significance or those without CH (median 56.5 vs 48.0 vs 47.0 years old, p=0.0077). After a median follow-up of 60.0 months after sampling, one patient with CML experienced relapse. Three-year Overall survival (94.2% vs. 92.9%, p=0.800) and cumulative incidence of second cancer (18.0% vs. 14.9%, p=0.410) after CH sampling were not associated with CH status. In conclusion, CH in HCT survivors is common and associated with donor age, transplantation for CML, and chronic graftversus-host disease.

43015369.title: Mediator kinase inhibition exposes a transcriptional vulnerability and synergizes with venetoclax in AML.
43015369.author: Aitchedji C
43015369.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous and aggressive hematologic malignancy associated with poor survival despite recent therapeutic advances. To identify novel anti-leukemic agents, we performed a high-throughput viability screen of 10,000 small molecules across 56 genetically diverse primary AML samples. Compounds with similar activity profiles were grouped into Compound Correlation Clusters (CCCs), leading to the identification of CCC163, which includes AML874, as a potent and selective hit. Integrated pharmacological and CRISPR-Cas9 approaches identified the Mediator complex as the molecular target of AML874. We demonstrated that AML874 acts as a selective CDK8/CDK19 inhibitor, disrupting Mediator-dependent transcription. FLT3-mutated AML showed increased sensitivity to AML874, suggesting a subtype-specific vulnerability. Notably, CDK8 inhibition synergized with venetoclax in AML cell lines and patient-derived xenograft models, resulting in enhanced anti-leukemic activity in vivo. Collectively, these findings establish CDK8/CDK19 inhibition as a therapeutically relevant strategy in AML.

43008231.title: International Cross-Age Consensus Guideline on Measurable Residual Disease Assessment in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
43008231.author: Kotrova M
43008231.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) assessment is central to risk stratification, response evaluation, and relapse detection in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). However, substantial global variability in its methodology and implementation persists. Differences in sampling strategies, detection methods, reporting thresholds, and interpretation criteria hinder cross-trial comparability and clinical standardization. To address this, an international expert panel representing major pediatric and adult study groups and reference laboratories developed consensus recommendations, using a structured current-practices survey followed by a multi-round Delphi process. Consensus was achieved on 38 of 41 statements. Recommendations span three domains: pre-analytical requirements, technical and nomenclature standards, and MRD-based remission and relapse definitions. Bone marrow was endorsed as the reference specimen for MRD assessment, and MRD was prioritized over cytomorphology in cases of discordance. Principles for risk- and actionability-guided late MRD monitoring, confirmation of MRD reappearance, and MRD-informed relapse assessment were also defined. Among the key technical consensus statements, a standardized MRD assay nomenclature was adopted. Areas without consensus-namely, anticoagulant choice for PCR-based MRD, interpretation of isolated BCR::ABL1 reconversion, and the exclusive use of MRD to define remission-highlight ongoing biological and clinical complexity. This guideline, applicable across all ages, provides a practical framework to standardize MRD assessment in ALL and support MRD-guided clinical decision-making.

43003869.title: Mesenchymal stromal cells drive immune escape in MDS and sAML through metabolic rewiring of NK cells.
43003869.author: Bisio V
43003869.abstract: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) are clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders that frequently progress to secondary acute myeloid leukemia (sAML). Besides intrinsic genetic changes, the disease's development is heavily influenced by the bone marrow (BM) microenvironment, especially mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs). In this study, we present a comprehensive characterization of how unhealthy MSCs affect natural killer (NK) cell anti-leukemic function in MDS and sAML. Using integrated ATAC-seq and RNA-seq profiling, we show that MDS/sAML-derived MSCs induce profound chromatin remodeling in NK cells, marked by reduced promoter accessibility and downregulation of genes essential for stress response and survival. Functionally, pathological MSCs fail to deliver the protective support normally provided by healthy MSCs, instead driving mitochondrial fragmentation and apoptosis in NK cells, ultimately suppressing their cytotoxic activity. Together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized loss of supportive capacity in pathological MSCs that hampers NK-cell fitness. Therapeutic approaches that bolster mitochondrial resilience in NK cells may help counteract this microenvironment-induced impairment and strengthen immune surveillance in MDS and sAML.

43020901.title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial.
43020901.author: Wirbel J
43020901.abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation can cure certain hematological disorders but has many complications. In retrospective studies, low gut microbiome diversity is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. In 2023, the Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1703 randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated the superiority of post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) and mycophenolate mofetil to tacrolimus and methotrexate (Tac/MTX) for graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis in participants with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. Here we report on the microbiome-focused companion study to 1703, Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1801, which coenrolled participants and shared trial registration. The primary endpoint was association between microbiome diversity at neutrophil engraftment and non-relapse mortality after 1 year; secondary endpoints included associations with other clinical outcomes and with baseline microbiome diversity. Based on 2575 longitudinally collected stool samples from 304 participants (Tac/MTX n = 147, PTCy n = 157), no association between engraftment microbiome diversity and non-relapse mortality was observed (P = 0.314), not meeting the primary endpoint. Lower baseline microbiome diversity was associated with shorter overall survival (P = 0.007). Safety data were reported in the original 1703 publication. In exploratory analyses, microbiome diversity and absolute microbial load were lower in PTCy compared to Tac/MTX on days 14-28 following HCT, independent of non-prophylaxis antibiotics exposure. Microbial domination events, when a single species exceeds 30% relative abundance, did not differ significantly between study arms and reflected both pathogen blooms and less severe disruptions of the microbial community. Clostridium scindens and secondary bile-acid metabolism pathways were less prevalent in PTCy than in Tac/MTX following HCT. In summary, we find prophylaxis regimens likely exert independent effects on both the microbiome and immune compartments and can also impact their interaction. Understanding whether and how microbiome-targeted interventions might improve transplant outcomes will therefore require careful disentangling of these effects within each specific treatment context. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03959241 .

43018998.author: Gribben JG

43018997.author: Roddie C

43016395.title: Intercellular transfer of FOLR2 from nurse-like cells fuels chronic lymphocytic leukemia cell activation and proliferation.
43016395.author: Domagala M
43016395.abstract: Communication with the lymphoid microenvironment is essential for the survival and proliferation of neoplastic B cells in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). While nurse-like cells (NLCs) are recognized as key components of this niche, the mechanisms and functional impact of their interactions with malignant cells remain insufficiently understood. Here, using primary patient cells, we found that NLCs express high levels of folate receptor beta (FOLR2), which correlate with increased survival of leukemic cells in vitro. Unexpectedly, we found that CLL cells acquire functional FOLR2 from NLCs via trogocytosis, enhancing their folate uptake. To further study the biological relevance of this phenomenon, we modeled lymphoid microenvironmental activation using CD40L and IL-15, which markedly increased FOLR2 transfer and induced robust NLC-dependent CLL cell activation and proliferation. These processes were closely associated, as FOLR2+ CLL cells represented the predominant population of actively cycling leukemic cells. Under the same conditions, we also observed an additional contact-independent mechanism of FOLR2 transfer, suggesting involvement of extracellular vesicles (EVs). To validate these findings in situ, we performed multiplex immunofluorescence analysis of CLL lymph nodes. This confirmed the presence of FOLR2⁺ NLCs and demonstrated their significant enrichment in more aggressive and proliferative cases. In addition, we detected FOLR2+ CLL cells in situ, supporting the occurrence of trogocytosis and possibly EVs mediated-transfer in the lymphoid microenvironment. Together, these results identify FOLR2 as a novel marker of protective NLCs and implicate trogocytosis with NLCs as an important mechanism that enhances CLL cell adaptation and promotes leukemic cell activation and proliferation.

43016387.title: Transcriptional landscape of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma and T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma: tumor microenvironment and checkpoint genes.
43016387.author: Kalashnikov I
43016387.abstract: Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) is a rare B-cell malignancy with an indolent course, yet some cases relapse or transform to Tcell/ histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma (THRLBCL). Biological factors underlying poor outcomes in NLPHL are largely unknown, and the relationship between THRLBCL and untransformed NLPHL has not been systematically defined. We analyzed 178 NLPHL and 22 THRLBCL cases using whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing and clinical data. NLPHL patients were younger, had limited-stage disease, and better outcomes than THRLBCL patients. Variant immuno-architectural patterns (IAP) in NLPHL showed THRLBCL-like transcriptional profiles, especially with splenic involvement and high Lymphocyte-Predominant International Prognostic Score (LP-IPS). In-silico deconvolution of the tumor microenvironment (TME) revealed B-cell enrichment in classic NLPHL, intermediate profiles in variant NLPHL, and increased activated CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells and macrophages in THRLBCL. Higher follicular helper T-cell content was associated with shorter event-free survival in an exploratory analysis. NLPHL cases showed strong B-cell and T-helper signatures, whereas THRLBCL cases were enriched for macrophage and cytotoxic T-cell pathways and expressed higher immune checkpoint genes, suggesting an immunosuppressive TME. Signatures defined a spectrum from classic to variant NLPHL and THRLBCL. External validation in independent cohorts reproduced this gradient, supporting a continuous microenvironmental spectrum spanning NLPHL and THRLBCL.

43008309.title: CD19-CD28 costimulatory bispecific antibody plus glofitamab in R/R B-NHL: a phase 1 dose-escalation study.
43008309.author: Dickinson MJ
43008309.abstract: RO7443904 (CD19-CD28) is a novel costimulatory bispecific antibody designed to enhance T-cell activation and anti-tumor activity when combined with the CD20xCD3 bispecific antibody glofitamab. We report primary results from a phase 1 dose-escalation trial (BP43131; NCT05219513) evaluating this combination in patients with relapsed/refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (B-NHL). In this study, 52 patients with heavily pre-treated B-NHL (aggressive, n = 33; indolent, n = 19) received obinutuzumab pretreatment to mitigate cytokine release syndrome, glofitamab step-up dosing (2.5/10/30 mg), and the addition of CD19-CD28 (initiated on cycle 1 day 10 or cycle 2 day 8), for up to 12 cycles. The primary objectives were safety, tolerability, and identification of the maximum tolerated dose, which was not reached. Key secondary and exploratory objectives included efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics. The most common adverse event (AE) was cytokine release syndrome (53.8%), which was predominantly low-grade and occurred primarily during glofitamab step-up (grade 1: 36.5%; grade 2: 19.2%; grade 4: 3.8%). Five fatal AEs (9.6%) were reported, all considered non-related to study treatment. The combination demonstrated substantial efficacy, with objective and complete response rates (ORR/CRR) of 63.6% and 42.4% for aggressive B-NHL, and 89.5% for both ORR and CRR in indolent B-NHL. Pharmacodynamic analyses confirmed CD19-CD28 enhanced and sustained T-cell proliferation and effector functions in peripheral blood. In conclusion, the combination of glofitamab with CD19-CD28 had a manageable safety profile and promising early efficacy in relapsed/refractory B-NHL, providing a strong clinical proof-of-concept for enhancing T-cell engager therapy with CD28 costimulation in B-NHL.

43008236.title: Is Circulating Tumor DNA Ready for Clinical Use in Large B-cell Lymphoma?
43008236.author: Merryman RW
43008236.abstract: Response assessment after frontline therapy for large B-cell lymphoma risk-stratifies patients into those at low risk for relapse and those with residual disease. Positron emission tomography scans form the cornerstone of the response criteria but cannot detect molecular-only disease. Circulating tumor DNA detects measurable residual disease (MRD) after therapy which is emerging as an adjunct tool for complex clinical decision-making. We discuss how MRD after therapy can be clinically implemented and additional data needed to unlock its full potential.

43006917.title: Pretreatment cognitive screening, treatment tolerability, and early mortality in older adults with advanced cancer initiating systemic therapy.
43006917.author: Mohamed M
43006917.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormal cognitive screening is common among older adults, yet its implications for cancer treatment tolerability remain unclear. We evaluated the association between pretreatment cognitive screening, treatment tolerability, and mortality among older adults with advanced cancer initiating systemic therapy.
METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the usual-care arm of the GAP70+ cluster-randomized clinical trial (NCT02054741). Participants were adults aged ≥70 years with incurable stage III/ IV solid tumors or lymphoma initiating high-risk systemic therapy. Pretreatment cognitive screening was assessed using Mini-Cog. Outcomes included grade 3-5 non-hematologic toxicity, unplanned hospitalization, and early treatment discontinuation within 3 months, and all-cause mortality at 6 months and 1 year. Multivariable logistic and Cox models adjusted for sociodemographic, clinical, and geriatric variables.
RESULTS: Among 368 patients (mean age 77.2 years), 32% had abnormal cognitive screening. Abnormal screening was associated with higher odds of unplanned hospitalization (OR = 1.79, 95% CI, 1.04-3.10). Age modified this association, with stronger effects among patients aged 70-79 years (OR = 3.16, 95% CI, 1.57-6.46) but not ≥80 years (OR = 0.72, 95% CI, 0.25-1.99). Abnormal screening was also associated with increased mortality at 6 months (HR = 1.94, 95% CI, 1.24-3.03) and 1 year (HR = 1.61, 95% CI, 1.16-2.24), but not with toxicity or early discontinuation.
CONCLUSIONS: Abnormal cognitive screening was associated with increased hospitalization and early mortality among older adults with advanced cancer receiving systemic therapy. Routine cognitive screening may improve risk stratification and treatment planning.

43002581.title: Terminal differentiation program of CD8 T cells guides immunotherapeutic options for CLL patients.
43002581.author: Camerini E
43002581.abstract: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) remains incurable and autologous T-cell-based therapies induce durable remissions in only a minority of patients. Although poor T-cell performance in CLL has been attributed to exhaustion, T cells from CLL patients retain cytokine production and lack key transcriptional markers of exhaustion, suggesting an alternative state of differentiation. Here, we performed an integrated phenotypic, epigenetic and functional analysis of circulating CD8⁺ T cells from treatment-naive CLL patients to define the nature and therapeutic relevance of terminal differentiation in CLL. CD8⁺ T cells from treatment-naive CLL patients were enriched for a terminally differentiated, CD27⁻CD28⁻CD57⁺KLRG1⁺ population with several senescence-associated features, including increased cell size, granularity, β-galactosidase activity, and reduced basal autophagy. However, these cells lacked key hallmarks of irreversible senescence. Instead, CLL T cells mounted robust but transient proliferative bursts and developed activation-associated γH2AX signals followed by impaired persistence and increased cell death upon repeated activation. Especially CD57⁺ T cells were vulnerable and incompatible with the experimental steps required for CAR T-cell manufacturing. The potent, acute effector function of these cells could, however, be harnessed by bispecific T-cell engagers, which induced effective cytolysis of both cell lines and primary CLL targets by these T cells. Collectively, our data support a model in which CD8+ T-cell dysfunction in CLL reflects accumulation of short-lived, terminally differentiated effector cells rather than canonical exhaustion or irreversible senescence. This state limits durable persistence required for CAR T-cell approached while preserving acute cytotoxicity relevant for bispecific antibody-based therapies in CLL.
