43002730.title: Modeling Long-Term Progression-Free Survival in Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma Treated With Daratumumab, Bortezomib, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone.
43002730.author: Sonneveld P
43002730.abstract: Daratumumab, bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (DVRd) significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) versus VRd in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) in transplant eligible (TE; PERSEUS) and transplant-ineligible (TIE; CEPHEUS) populations. Median PFS with DVRd has not been reached in either study. This analysis extrapolated PFS data from PERSEUS and CEPHEUS (TIE subgroup) to estimate long-term outcomes for DVRd. Following UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guidance on survival data extrapolation, seven parametric distributions were fitted to model PFS data. In PERSEUS (TE population), the projected median PFS range across distributions was 158-255 months versus 76-119 months and best-fit (exponential distribution) PFS estimates were 205 months (17.1 [range, 13.2-21.2] years, DVRd) versus 87 months (7.3 [range, 6.3-9.9] years, VRd). For CEPHEUS (TIE population), projected median PFS range across distributions was 96-118 months versus 52-54 months and best-fit estimates were 100 months (8.3 [range, 8.0-9.8] years, DVRd) versus 53 months (4.4 [range, 4.3-4.5] years, VRd). PFS projections were significantly longer with DVRd than VRd in TE (additional 118 months; 9.8 years) and TIE patients (additional 47 months; 3.9 years) across all seven distributions. These extrapolations reinforce the benefit of DVRd as standard of care in NDMM regardless of transplant eligibility.

43002727.title: Monoclonal Gammopathy of Neurologic Significance: A Practical Framework for Diagnosis and Management.
43002727.author: Bhutani M
43002727.abstract: Monoclonal gammopathy of neurologic significance (MGNS) refers to peripheral neuropathies that are attributable to a monoclonal immunoglobulin produced by an underlying clonal plasma cell population or B-cell population in the absence of multiple myeloma, amyloid light chain amyloidosis, or polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal protein, skin changes syndrome. Because the prevalence of both monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and peripheral neuropathy increases with age, their coexistence is frequently incidental. However, population-based studies demonstrate a significantly higher risk of neuropathy among patients with MGUS compared with matched controls. Establishing causality requires careful clinical phenotyping, correlation with electrodiagnostic studies, and systematic exclusion of alternative and potentially life-threatening causes that require urgent intervention. This review presents a practical, stepwise diagnostic and therapeutic framework for MGNS, emphasizing multidisciplinary collaboration between hematology and neurology. The approach is illustrated through two representative clinical scenarios: IgM MGUS with anti-myelin-associated glycoprotein (anti-MAG) neuropathy and non-IgM MGUS with chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) or its variants. Treatment approaches differ fundamentally between these subtypes. B-cell-directed therapy with rituximab is the most commonly used first-line treatment for IgM anti-MAG neuropathy, whereas non-IgM MGNS with CIDP is managed with immunomodulatory strategies including intravenous immunoglobulin, corticosteroids, and plasmapheresis. We also discuss novel therapeutics, including Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors and complement-directed therapies. This framework provides clinicians with a structured approach to assess causal likelihood, stratify patients by neuropathy subtype, and guide evidence-based treatment decisions across the MGNS spectrum.

43002606.title: Detection, Monitoring, and Discrimination of Amyloidogenic vs Innocent Light Chains in Systemic Amyloidoses.
43002606.author: Palladini G
43002606.abstract: Immunoglobulin light chains (LCs) span the spectrum of B-cell clonal disorders from monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance to multiple myeloma and Waldenström macroglobulinemia. Beyond serving as disease markers, monoclonal immunoglobulins can cause organ damage in monoclonal gammopathies of clinical significance (MGCS). In AL amyloidosis the pathogenic agent is a monoclonal light chain (LC). AL amyloidosis is a treatable yet rapidly progressive condition in which early diagnosis is critical for organ preservation and survival. High-sensitivity laboratory tools for detection of amyloidogenic LCs are essential in diagnosis, while precise quantitative methods are required for monitoring treatment response and for identifying relapse, where standardized relapse definitions remain an unmet need. With increasingly effective therapies, deep hematologic response assessment and measurable residual disease detection-through mass spectrometry-based methods, flow cytometry, and next-generation sequencing-are central to decision-making. Emerging strategies to discriminate "innocent" from amyloidogenic LCs will enable pre-symptomatic intervention in patients with apparently benign monoclonal gammopathies. These approaches include biomarkers of early organ damage and LC-intrinsic features that enhance amyloid propensity (N-glycosylation, preferential germline gene usage, and reduced stability). Such tools also hold promise for the differential diagnosis of non-AL amyloidoses, particularly transthyretin (ATTR) cardiac amyloidosis-the most common form in elderly males and African-American populations-who are at elevated risk of coexisting LC-producing clones. Rapid and accurate exclusion of AL amyloidosis in this setting is now a clinical imperative. This review synthesizes current laboratory approaches and future directions for LC detection and monitoring in systemic amyloidoses, highlighting their impact on hematologic practice.

43009481.title: Impact of socioeconomic status on treatment and survival in multiple myeloma in Australia.
43009481.author: Gration B
43009481.abstract: Outcomes in multiple myeloma (MM) have improved significantly but remain heterogeneous. We assessed the impact of non-biological social determinants of health on treatment and survival outcomes in Australia using data from the Australian and New Zealand Myeloma and Related Diseases Registry. A total of 4405 patients diagnosed with MM between June 2012 and October 2025 across 44 Australian sites were assigned an area-level socioeconomic status (SES) using individual postcodes. Baseline characteristics, treatment and survival outcomes were compared across high (n = 1484), medium (n = 1463), and low (n = 1458) SES tertiles. Lower neighbourhood SES was associated with higher BMI, poorer functional status, more comorbidities (diabetes, cardiac and pulmonary disease), Asian ethnicity and greater remoteness. Independent of these baseline differences, patients from lower SES neighbourhoods were less likely to receive an autologous stem cell transplant (odds ratio = 1.1 medium vs low, p = 0.41; 1.5 high vs low, p < 0.01) and time to reach ASCT following induction was longer (p < 0.001) despite this being standard-of-care therapy with proven survival benefit. Median overall survival was shorter for the low SES group at 78.5 months compared to 92.5 months (HR = 0.85, p = 0.01) and 86.7 months (HR = 0.85, p = 0.01) for the medium and high SES groups respectively. These findings demonstrate significant disparities in treatment and outcomes favouring higher SES, independent of biological factors, within a universal healthcare system. This suggests that non-biological factors continue to influence access to standard-of-care therapy and survival, warranting further research to identify and address barriers to equitable care.

43003799.title: Infectious complications following bispecific antibody or CAR T therapy in adult patients with hematologic malignancies: a retrospective database analysis.
43003799.author: Michael M
43003799.abstract: T-cell redirection therapies, including bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T therapy, have transformed the treatment of relapsed or refractory hematologic malignancies. However, comparative data on infectious complications between these treatments remain limited. We performed a propensity score-matched analysis of adults with hematologic malignancies treated with BsAbs or CAR T using the TriNetX global research network. To mitigate confounding, we utilized 1:1 propensity score matching (caliper 0.1) to balance cohorts on demographics, malignancy type, comorbidities, and prior treatments. The primary outcome was 1-year infection hazard in BsAbs vs. CAR T. We included 2 192 matched patients (1 096/group; mean age 65.8 (11.4) years for BsAbs, 65.4 (10.2) years for CAR T). Multiple myeloma was the most common malignancy (~62%). At 1 year, infection hazard was not statistically different between cohorts (BsAbs: 57% vs. CAR T: 55.9%; HR: 1.07; 95% CI: [0.96-1.20]). Early phase infection hazard (days 1-30) was lower with BsAbs but not statistically significant (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: [0.74-1.02]). However, BsAbs therapy was associated with higher infection hazard during intermediate (days 31-180; HR: 1.27; 95% CI: [1.10-1.46]) and late phases (days 181-365; HR: 1.20; 95% CI: [1.01-1.41]). In the late phase, BsAbs carried higher hazard for fungal (HR: 2.14; 95% CI: [1.26-3.64]) and viral pathogens (HR: 1.32; 95% CI: [1.02-1.73]). Respiratory tract infections were the most frequent complication and were higher with BsAbs across all time windows (1-year: 35.4% vs. 30.4%; HR: 1.32; 95% CI: [1.14-1.53]). In conclusion, among patients captured within TriNetX, the overall observed 1-year infection rate did not differ significantly between BsAbs and CAR T therapy. However, BsAbs therapy was associated with higher coded rates of late-onset infections after extensive adjustment, although residual confounding from disease severity and treatment duration remains possible. Further studies must better define this infection burden and optimize prevention strategies.

43033550.title: Emerging molecular probes for lung cancer: Targets, translational evidence, and theranostic potential.
43033550.author: Yu Z
43033550.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer incidence and mortality worldwide, and the management of both non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC) has entered the era of precision medicine.
METHODS: This review summarizes current progress in radiolabeled molecular probes for lung cancer. Radiotracers were categorized according to their molecular targets, with emphasis on design strategies, preclinical and clinical evidence, current limitations, and potential theranostic applications.
RESULTS: Evidence ranged from preclinical studies to validated diagnostic or predictive performance, with occasional management changes. EGFR and FAPI imaging supported mutation assessment, response prediction, and staging, while immune-targeted probes characterized checkpoint heterogeneity and immune-cell distribution. MET, HER2, folate receptor alpha, and CXCR4 imaging showed early human feasibility; ALK and CTLA-4 imaging remained predominantly preclinical. Choline and FLT imaging assessed metabolism and early pharmacodynamic responses. Theranostic strategies enabled target confirmation and dosimetry, with FAPI-directed therapy entering clinical investigation and CXCR4-, CD133-, and DLL3-directed therapies showing preclinical efficacy. Translation still requires standardized thresholds, prospective validation, and evidence of benefit from imaging-guided decisions.
CONCLUSIONS: Molecular probes should be advanced according to the clinical decision they are intended to inform, not target expression alone. Prospective trials must compare imaging-guided pathways with FDG PET/CT and tissue-based standards and must measure downstream treatment selection and patient-important outcomes before routine implementation.

43025701.title: Final analysis from PECATI phase 2 trial, lenvatinib in combination with pembrolizumab in pretreated advanced B3-thymoma and thymic carcinoma.
43025701.author: Remon J
43025701.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is no standard second-line treatment for patients with platinum-refractory advanced B3-Thymoma (T) and thymic carcinoma (TC). In this population, the PECATI trial (NCT04710628) testing the combination lenvatinib and pembrolizumab met its primary endpoint, with 5-month progression-free survival (PFS) of 88.0%. Here we report the final clinical study results.
METHODS: PECATI is a single-arm, phase 2 trial enrolling patients with metastatic B3-T and TC, without autoimmune disorders that have progressed following at least one platinum-based chemotherapy. The trial evaluated lenvatinib (20 mg orally once daily) plus pembrolizumab (200 mg iv infusion once every 3 weeks) in 3-week cycles for a maximum of 35 cycles if no disease progression or toxicity.
RESULTS: 43 patients were enrolled: median age 57 years (33-81); 84% had a TC; 65% Masaoka Koga IVB, 51.2% of patients with ≥3 metastatic sites, and 44.2% received ≥2 prior lines for advanced disease. After a median follow-up of 24.6 months, the median PFS was 22.1 months (95%CI: 10.9-25.1), and the median overall survival (OS) was 40.2 months (95%CI: 19.1-not estimated), with 36-month OS rate of 53.0%. The confirmed ORR was 25.6% and median duration of response was not reached. The rate of grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events was 44.2% leading to treatment discontinuation in 27.9% of cases. Two (4.7%) non-treatment-related grade 5 events were reported. The rate of grade 3 immune-related adverse events was 11.6%.
CONCLUSION: The final results of PECATI trial supports the combination lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab as a potential treatment option in pre-treated advanced B3-thymoma and thymic carcinoma. Toxicity profile is manageable but close monitoring is advised.

43014696.title: Clinicogenomic determinants of early progression on first-line osimertinib in EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
43014696.author: Pecci F
43014696.abstract:
BACKGROUND: With the recent approvals of the FLAURA2 and MARIPOSA regimens in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), identifying clinico-genomic features predictive of suboptimal outcomes with first-line osimertinib monotherapy is critical in guiding upfront treatment selections.
METHODS: This is a multicenter retrospective study enrolling patients with advanced NSCLC harboring common EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions [ex19del], L858R) treated with first-line osimertinib monotherapy across 13 centers (Clinical cohort). Comprehensive baseline genomic data on tumor tissue were available for DFCI and MSKCC (Genomic cohort). The association of clinicogenomic features with real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) was investigated. Caris Life Science cohort was used for RNA-sequencing analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 1488 patients were enrolled in the clinical cohort; at median follow-up of 43.3 months, median rwPFS was 16.3 months (95%CI 15.3-17.4), median overall survival was 36.7 months (95%CI 34.8-39.4). TP53 mutated (TP53MUT) was independently associated with shorter rwPFS compared with TP53 wild-type (TP53WT), specifically in EGFR ex19del (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.68, p<0.001) than in L858R subgroup (aHR 1.18, p=0.2). Using a survROC model for rwPFS, PD-L1 was the variable with greatest impact on risk of progression at 6 (ΔAUC=0.0549) and 12 (ΔAUC=0.0348) months. In the genomic cohort, patients with TSGMUT (RBM10, CREBBP, ATM, RB1, KMT2D, TSC2, PTEN) had shorted rwPFS compared to TSGWT (aHR 1.5, p=0.01), specifically in L858R subgroup (aHR 1.8, p=0.02). Combining TP53 with TSG, pts with TP53MUT plus at least one TSGMUT and pts with TP53WT-TSGMUT had shorter rwPFS compared to TP53WT-TSGWT and TP53MUT-TSGWT. In the genomic cohort, PD-L1 TPS was the strongest predictor of very-early rwPFS (ΔAUC=0.16), followed by TP53-TSG (ΔAUC=0.08). PD-L1 was associated with higher MET mRNA and immunohistochemistry expression and transcriptional program enriched for proliferative, inflammatory, and metabolic signaling pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter real-world cohort, baseline PD-L1 and TP53 combined with TSG predict very-early progression to first-line osimertinib, with EGFR subtype-specific prognostic impact of genomic co-alterations.

43019607.title: Patient factors affecting unplanned admission or emergency department attendance following systemic anti-cancer therapy for advanced non-small cell lung cancer: A population-based retrospective cohort study.
43019607.author: Steventon L
43019607.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Systemic anti-cancer therapy (SACT) for patients in advanced stages of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) can increase early treatment-related mortality, toxicities, and unplanned hospital admissions or emergency department attendance. We sought to understand admission/emergency attendance rates and patient factors associated with these events in England.
METHODS: This retrospective, population-based cohort study described rates of unplanned admission/emergency department attendance within 30 days of first SACT for advanced-stage NSCLC patients treated 2015-2019. Associations of patient, treatment and regional characteristics with admissions were investigated using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of 22,521 included patients, 35% (N = 7,870) had an unplanned admission/emergency attendance within 30 days of first SACT, with 20% dying within 30 days of this admission (N = 1,616/7,870). Seventy-one percent did not receive any further SACT treatment (N = 5,600/7,870). Fifty-four percent previously had an unplanned admission/emergency attendance in the three months before starting SACT (N = 4,225/7,870), and this was associated with increased 30-day admission/emergency department attendance in multivariable logistic regression analysis (OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.53, 1.72, P < 0.001). Unplanned 30-day admission/emergency attendance increased with worsening performance status (PS0 = 28%, PS1 = 34%, PS ≥ 2 = 45%, P < 0.001). Two-year overall mortality was 73%.
CONCLUSION: Over one third of patients treated with SACT for advanced NSCLC had an unplanned admission/emergency attendance within 30-days of treatment initiation, with high mortality and treatment discontinuation rates in these patients. Prior hospitalisation and poor performance status were the strongest indicators for admission. These findings can support tailored approaches to support patients and minimise risk of adverse events and hospitalisation.

43003045.title: Heterogeneous response and progression patterns during tarlatamab therapy in relapsed small cell lung cancer.
43003045.author: Murata S
43003045.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tarlatamab has demonstrated activity in relapsed small cell lung cancer (SCLC). However, lesion-level response heterogeneity and organ-specific patterns of progression during tarlatamab therapy remain poorly characterized in clinical practice.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients with relapsed SCLC treated with tarlatamab between June 2021 and March 2026. Overall response at the first radiological evaluation and best overall response were assessed according to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Lesion-level response patterns at the first radiological assessment were categorized as responsive, mixed response, stable, or progressive. Progression sites, intracranial lesion changes, and progression-free survival (PFS) were analyzed. Site-specific findings were summarized at the first evaluation and at overall progressive disease (PD).
RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients were included. Mixed response was observed in 11 (37.9%) patients and across the RECIST response categories at the first radiological evaluation. The median PFS was 3.2 months and was longest in the responsive group, intermediate in the mixed-response group, and shortest in the progressive group. Among 15 patients evaluable for intracranial response, seven experienced at least 30% intracranial tumor shrinkage at the first assessment, and four subsequently developed intracranial progression. Among 20 patients with disease progression, 12 had progression at three or more sites. Site-specific assessments showed that decreased or stable disease could coexist with overall PD.
CONCLUSION: Tarlatamab showed heterogeneous response and progression patterns in relapsed SCLC, including frequent mixed response and intracranial progression. Lesion-level assessment may provide a more comprehensive characterization of disease behavior during tarlatamab therapy.

43003044.title: Lung cancer detection beyond screening eligibility through an incidental lung nodule program.
43003044.author: Wang HY
43003044.abstract:
PURPOSE: Lung cancer screening has improved early detection among individuals who meet established age and smoking criteria. However, many patients who develop lung cancer remain ineligible for screening. Incidental pulmonary nodules (ILN) identified on imaging performed for other indications may provide important complementary pathway for early lung cancer detection, but the contribution of structured ILN programs to cancer detection outside conventional screening eligibility remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected data from two urban academic hospitals from January 2023 through January 4, 2026. Patients with ILN requiring surveillance were identified using natural language processing of radiology reports and navigator review. Screening eligibility was classified according to 2021 United States Preventive Services Task Force criteria. Cancer detection, stage, histology, treatment, and factors associated with cancer among screening-ineligible patients were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 2,804 patients requiring follow-up, 2,248 (80.2 %) were screening ineligible, 466 (16.6 %) eligible, and 90 (3.2 %) unclassified. Lung cancer was diagnosed in 73 patients (2.6 %), including 44 (60.3 %) who were screening ineligible. Of these, 15 were never-smokers and 29 were former or current smokers who did not meet screening criteria. Thirty-six (81.8 %) had stage 0-II disease, 21 (47.7 %) underwent definitive surgical resection, and 36 (81.8 %) had adenocarcinoma. Nodule diameter > 8 mm was associated with lung cancer diagnosis (adjusted odds ratio 15.89; 95 % CI 5.24-71.47).
CONCLUSIONS: The ILN program identified substantial early-stage, clinically actionable lung cancers among patients outside conventional screening eligibility. The high proportion of early-stage diagnoses and definitive resections supports ILN programs as a complementary pathway to organized lung cancer screening.

43003719.title: A Wide pCR Divide: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy versus targeted therapy in resectable NSCLC.
43003719.author: Li R

43033551.title: Treatment-cycle-resolved peripheral blood T-cell GP73 dynamics are associated with clinical benefit during PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-based therapy in NSCLC.
43033551.author: Feng X
43033551.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Single-time-point tissue-based biomarkers incompletely capture evolving immune states during immunotherapy. This study aimed to dynamically characterize associations linking GP73 levels in peripheral blood T cells and serum to PD‑1/PD-L1 inhibitor response and clinical outcomes in NSCLC patients treated with PD‑1/PD-L1 inhibitor-based therapy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Intracellular T-cell GP73 was quantified by flow cytometry in available samples from 76 patients from baseline through up to eight cycles. Early sampling was days 1-7; late sampling was day 18 until before the next administration. Mixed-effects models, ROC analyses, and delayed-entry Cox regression assessed dynamics, prespecified study-defined clinical benefit, and progression-free survival (PFS), respectively. Conventional RECIST 1.1 objective response was a sensitivity endpoint.
RESULTS: T-cell GP73 declined within cycles (P = 0.012) and rebounded between cycles (P < 0.001). Between-cycle changes differed by clinical benefit status (interaction P < 0.001), unlike within-cycle changes (interaction P = 0.181). T-cell GP73 was higher with clinical benefit (both P < 0.001), with early- and late-window AUCs of 0.865 and 0.772, respectively. RECIST 1.1 sensitivity analyses retained a between-cycle interaction (P = 0.005) and early- and late-window objective-response discrimination (AUCs = 0.761 and 0.808). Serum GP73 showed limited discrimination (AUC = 0.571) and no significant correlation with T-cell GP73 (P = 0.432). Higher late-window T-cell GP73 was associated with longer PFS (delayed-entry Cox HR per 100-MFI increase = 0.63, 95 % CI 0.44-0.93; P = 0.018).
CONCLUSION: Treatment-cycle-resolved T-cell GP73 monitoring revealed clinical benefit-associated dynamics, while L-window GP73 levels were associated with clinical benefit and progression-free survival in NSCLC.

43008663.title: Coexistence of Osimertinib-Resistant and Osimertinib-Sensitive cell states in an EGFR-Mutant NSCLC model derived at osimertinib resistance.
43008663.author: Chillico IC
43008663.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is a standard first-line treatment for EGFR-mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), but acquired resistance remains a clinical challenge. Resistance involves genetic mechanisms and non-genetic cell-state transitions, including epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) plasticity and drug-tolerant persister phenotypes. Patient-derived models established at disease progression may better capture clinically relevant resistance mechanisms.
METHODS: We established LIBM-ADK-11 from the pleural effusion of a patient with EGFR exon 19p.Leu747_Pro753delinsSer-mutant NSCLC progressing on osimertinib. Cells were studied at low and high passages and fractionated by CD44 expression into CD44-positive/P2 and CD44-negative/P4 subpopulations. EGFR mutation status, CD44 expression, transcriptomics, growth, osimertinib sensitivity, EGFR signaling, sphere formation, cell-cycle distribution and pemetrexed response were evaluated.
RESULTS: LIBM-ADK-11 retained the EGFR mutation during long-term culture. CD44 sorting identified two phenotypically distinct cell states. CD44-positive P2 cells were enriched for extracellular matrix remodeling, EMT-like, inflammatory, CAF-like and macrophage/TAM-mimicry programs, with increased glycolysis-related signatures, slower growth, higher metabolic activity and osimertinib resistance. CD44-negative P4 cells displayed a more epithelial profile, cholesterol-associated gene expression and greater osimertinib sensitivity. Osimertinib inhibited EGFR phosphorylation in both populations, indicating that P2 resistance was not explained by persistent EGFR signaling. Long-term culture favored loss of CD44-positive cells, whereas osimertinib delayed this loss and preferentially depleted the CD44-negative fraction. Pemetrexed partially reduced both compartments.
CONCLUSIONS: LIBM-ADK-11 is a clinically relevant model of osimertinib-resistant EGFR-mutant NSCLC in which CD44-positive drug-tolerant and CD44-negative drug-sensitive states coexist. These findings highlight phenotypic heterogeneity as a potential determinant of osimertinib resistance and support strategies addressing distinct cellular states at disease progression.

43025364.title: Characteristics and outcomes of patients with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer harboring a HER2-activating mutation: a real-world retrospective cohort study using a US clinico-genomic database.
43025364.author: Le X
43025364.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2/ERBB2) mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment options.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health records from US academic and community cancer centers to describe characteristics and treatments of patients with HER2-mutated locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC initiating first-line (1 L) therapy between January 1, 2015, and March 31, 2024, in a real-world setting. Endpoints included real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) and overall survival (OS) by line of therapy and in subgroups of interest.
RESULTS: Of 158 patients included (median age 69 years, 43.0% with Y772_A775dup [YVMA] mutation), 50.6% had ≥ 2 lines of therapy. Common 1 L therapies were chemotherapy + immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI; 36.1%) and chemotherapy (27.8%); common second-line (2 L) therapies were ICI (23.8%), chemotherapy + ICI (16.3%), and HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC; 16.3%). Median rwPFS/OS was 5.7/17.5, and 4.3/11.2 months, following initiation of 1 L and 2 L treatment, respectively. Median rwPFS ranged from 4.4 to 8.9 months and median OS from 15.7 to 16.0 months, following initiation of 1 L chemotherapy with or without ICI. Median rwPFS following initiation of 2 L treatment with ICI ± chemotherapy, chemotherapy ± monoclonal antibody, or HER2-targeted ADC ranged from 3.0 to 4.7 months, and OS from 10.8 to 23.4 months. Outcomes appeared to be descriptively inferior in patients with YVMA mutations versus other subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall outcomes were unsatisfactory, including in patients who had received chemotherapy ± ICI or HER2-targeted ADC in any line, highlighting the need for more effective targeted therapies.

43006889.title: Occupational solar ultraviolet radiation exposure and incident ocular melanoma risk in two large-scale nordic cohorts.
43006889.author: Turner MC
43006889.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Solar radiation is a ubiquitous human carcinogen however its role in the etiology of cancer beyond melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancer is unclear. We sought to investigate the role of occupational solar ultraviolet radiation (UVR) exposure in ocular melanoma, a rare malignancy, using data from two large-scale Northern European cohorts.
METHODS: The Danish DOC*X cohort followed 2.95 million participants for a mean (SD) of 19.3 (11.2) years (1977 to 2015). The Norwegian Nor-Work cohort followed 2.45 million participants for a mean (SD) of 30.7 (13.6) years (1961 to 2020). Cancer cases were ascertained through national cancer registries. Lifetime cumulative occupational solar UVR exposure in terms of standard erythema dose (SED) was estimated using a novel European quantitative job-exposure matrix.
RESULTS: There were 233 incident ocular melanoma cases in DOC*X and 581 in Nor-Work. In DOC*X, there was little clear evidence for an association. In Nor-Work, adjusted incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were similarly elevated in the 2nd to 4th quartiles compared with the 1st (reference) quartile, being 1.80 (95% CI 1.12 to 2.92), 1.63 (95% CI 0.99 to 2.69), and 1.72 (95% CI 1.03 to 2.89), respectively (p-trend = 0.06) with an IRR per interquartile increase of 1.05 (95% CI 0.92 to 1.18). For uveal melanoma, IRRs among quartile categories were also elevated although weaker ranging from 1.35 to 1.45.
CONCLUSIONS: We observed some non-monotonic positive associations of occupational solar UVR exposure and ocular melanoma particularly in Norway. Efforts to advance exposure assessment for large-scale studies are warranted.

43013345.title: SPROUT Guidelines for Molecular Profiling for Children with Solid Tumors: A Consensus Recommendation from the American Association for Cancer Research.
43013345.author: Gestrich C
43013345.abstract:
PURPOSE: Molecular diagnostics are standard of care for most adults with solid malignancies, but implementation in pediatric solid tumors remains inconsistent. The SPROUT (Somatic Profiling for Pediatric Cancer Refining our Understanding and Treatment) Molecular Guidelines Working Group was convened to develop molecular testing guidelines for pediatric solid tumors.
EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: A structured literature review was performed using Covidence to identify relevant clinical studies evaluating molecular diagnostics in pediatric solid tumors. The literature and collective clinical experience of the multidisciplinary working group were used to develop consensus recommendations for molecular profiling at diagnosis and at relapse or recurrence.
RESULTS: Of 361 manuscripts screened, 41 studies were included for data extraction. Based on the available evidence and expert consensus, recommendations were developed for the use and timing of DNA and RNA next-generation sequencing and methylation profiling across pediatric solid tumors.
CONCLUSIONS: The SPROUT Molecular Guidelines provide a framework for standardized implementation of molecular diagnostics in pediatric solid tumors. Broad adoption of these recommendations may improve diagnostic precision, reduce variability in molecular testing, and increase opportunities for biomarker-directed therapy and clinical trial enrollment for children with cancer.

43033043.title: Cross-ancestry proteome-wide mendelian randomization of plasma proteins and breast cancer susceptibility.
43033043.author: Wu X
43033043.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The plasma proteome may help connect inherited breast cancer susceptibility to biologically interpretable and potentially actionable pathways, but proteome-wide evidence across ancestries remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses of breast cancer risk using cis-protein quantitative trait loci for 1,962 distinct plasma proteins from 34,557 European-ancestry participants in the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project. Breast cancer genome-wide association studies included 156,901 cases and 204,634 controls of European, East Asian, and African ancestries. Ancestry-specific MR estimates were combined by fixed-effects meta-analysis. Candidate proteins were further evaluated through subtype-specific and reverse-direction MR analyses, statistical colocalization, replication in independent European and East Asian proteomic datasets, and analyses of associations between protein polygenic scores and breast cancer status in All of Us.
RESULTS: Twelve proteins achieved Bonferroni significance in the cross-ancestry meta-analysis (P < 0.05/1,971 tests), including eight previously reported proteins and four newly prioritized by MR. DNPH1 showed cross-ancestry heterogeneity, while CASP8, RALB, and USP28 showed cross-subtype heterogeneity after accounting for shared controls (all P < 0.05/12). Complementary support varied: six candidates showed strong colocalization (PPH4 ≥ 0.80); four replicated with a consistent direction and nominal significance in deCODE, two in the Japan COVID-19 Task Force, and four in All of Us (all P < 0.05). The strongest cumulative support was observed for LRRC25, PARK7, and LRRC37A2.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings prioritize circulating protein candidates for mechanistic, prevention-oriented, and translational follow-up in breast cancer, while underscoring the need for larger ancestrally diverse proteomic resources to support equitable target and biomarker discovery.

43023429.title: Geographic Variation In Long-Term PM2.5 Exposure and Lung Cancer Incidence in the United States.
43023429.author: Myers S
43023429.abstract:
PURPOSE: A growing share of lung cancers occur in people who have never smoked, and air pollution may be one contributor. Inhalable particulate matter less than 2.5 um in diameter (PM2.5) has been linked to adverse health effects, but its role in lung cancer development across regions of the United States remains unclear.
METHODS: Lung cancer incidence from 2018-2022 (via Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) and annual average PM2.5 from 2005-2009 and 2010-2014 (via Area Health Resource File) were studied. Ordinary least squares (OLS) and geographically weighted regression (GWR) models were run, and models were compared using the corrected Akaike information criterion (AICc). Covariates included county-level poverty, racial makeup, educational attainment, and prevalence of smoking. Geographic distribution of PM2.5 levels was mapped to identify spatial clustering of higher and lower exposure (hot and cold spots) using the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic.
RESULTS: For both time windows, PM2.5 exposure was positively associated with lung cancer incidence. GWR models demonstrated improved model fit relative to OLS across both PM2.5 exposure periods (2005-2009: AICc 20,892 vs 21,810; 2010-2014: AICc 20,883 vs 21,847). Local GWR coefficient estimates for PM2.5 varied across counties, indicating spatial heterogeneity in the association between PM2.5 exposure and lung cancer incidence.
CONCLUSION: The relationship between PM2.5 exposure and lung cancer incidence varies spatially, with different levels of risk in different counties. These exploratory findings show where the association appears stronger or weaker; they are a starting point for further study rather than a basis for county-specific interventions.

43019708.title: Risk factors for early-onset cancers: Results from the JANUS cohort in Norway.
43019708.author: Botteri E
43019708.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of early-onset cancers, defined as cancers diagnosed before 50 years of age, is increasing worldwide. Identifying the underlying causes and potential preventive strategies has therefore become an urgent public health priority.
METHODS: We selected individuals aged 18-49 years (70.6% age 40-44) enrolled in the Janus Serum Bank Cohort in Norway from 1972 to 2002. We used Cox regression models to assess the association of sociodemographic, lifestyle, anthropometric, clinical and biochemical variables with the risk of early-onset cancers, overall and by the most common cancer types.
RESULTS: We included 144,907 men and 132,136 women. After a median follow-up of 8.7 years, we observed 1921 total early-onset cancer cases in men and 3563 in women, including 1356 breast cancers. Overall, female sex, increasing age and height, non-married status, being underweight, cigarette smoking, and hypertension were associated with an increased risk of early-onset cancer, whereas moderate-to-high physical activity, both in sport (borderline significant) and occupational, was associated with a decreased risk. Obesity was associated with a lower risk of total early-onset cancer, largely driven by the association observed for breast cancer, however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously. Diabetes was suggestively associated with an increased risk of early-onset cancers among never smokers. When exploring individual cancer types, several site-specific associations emerged.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results identify several factors associated with early-onset cancer risk and suggest a potential role for modifiable behaviours, such as smoking and physical activity, as targets in prevention strategies.

43021552.title: Olanzapine or prochlorperazine added to antiemetic therapy for persistent chemotherapy-induced nausea: an NCORP phase 3 RCT.
43021552.author: Peppone LJ
43021552.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite guideline-consistent antiemetic prophylaxis, persistent chemotherapy-induced nausea remains common, and comparative phase 3 evidence for olanzapine versus prochlorperazine is limited. We evaluated whether adding olanzapine or prochlorperazine to standardized Cycle 2 antiemetic prophylaxis reduces persistent nausea compared with placebo.
METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 23 NCORP community oncology sites (April 2018-January 2024), women 18 years or older with breast cancer receiving moderately or highly emetogenic chemotherapy who recorded a Cycle 1 nausea score of 3 or greater (1-7 scale) were randomized 1:1:1 during Cycle 2 to placebo, prochlorperazine (10 mg every 8 hours, Days 1-4), or olanzapine (10 mg once daily, Days 1-4), added to netupitant/palonosetron plus dexamethasone. The primary outcome was change in average nausea from Cycle 1 to Cycle 2; the key secondary outcome was change in maximum nausea.
RESULTS: Among 1363 screened patients, 310 comprised the intention-to-treat population (placebo, 91; prochlorperazine, 110; olanzapine, 109). Compared with placebo, average nausea improved with prochlorperazine (between-group difference, -0.44; P=.01) and olanzapine (-0.57; P=.001). Olanzapine reduced maximum nausea more than prochlorperazine (difference, -0.59; P=.02) and improved FACT-G quality-of-life scores over placebo (difference, 4.91; P=.006) and prochlorperazine (5.80; P=.001). Adverse events were primarily grade 1-2, with no toxicity-related discontinuations.
CONCLUSIONS: Adding olanzapine or prochlorperazine to standardized Cycle 2 antiemetic prophylaxis reduced persistent chemotherapy-induced nausea compared with placebo. Olanzapine produced greater improvement in maximum nausea and quality of life than prochlorperazine and is an effective escalation option, with prochlorperazine a reasonable alternative when olanzapine is unsuitable.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03367572.

43014812.title: Longitudinal Kidney Function Trajectories and Their Association With Hemoglobin and Transfusion Phenotype in Adults With β-Thalassemia.
43014812.author: Gianesin B
43014812.abstract: Renal functional trajectories and their associations with hemoglobin exposure remain incompletely characterized in adults with β-thalassemia. We analyzed 994 adults (806 transfusion-dependent thalassemia [TDT], 188 non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia [NTDT]) followed in the Italian Webthal network for up to 16 years. eGFR was estimated using CKD-EPI 2021 and analyzed using mixed-effects models. Baseline hyperfiltration was present in 22%, but was not associated with significantly faster subsequent eGFR decline. Overall eGFR declined by -1.13 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI, -1.20 to -1.07), with a steeper trajectory in TDT than NTDT. In 877 patients (5529 observations), models incorporating one-year-lagged, time-varying hemoglobin and baseline eGFR showed that hemoglobin-eGFR associations differed across transfusion phenotypes. Among phenoconverted patients, higher lagged hemoglobin was associated with a more negative age-related eGFR slope, persisting in sensitivity analyses accounting for baseline eGFR. Adjustment for hemoglobin did not eliminate phenotype-related differences in slopes. Chelation regimen was not associated with slope differences in the selected long-term monotherapy subgroup. Thus, renal trajectories vary by transfusion phenotype, and their associations with hemoglobin exposure are heterogeneous. Whether declining eGFR reflects attenuation of hyperfiltration or progressive renal injury cannot be established from these observational data.

43008228.title: Nuclear Receptor Nur77 Orchestrates Hematopoietic Lineage Commitment to Avert Anemia in Diabetes.
43008228.author: Huang QL
43008228.abstract: Anemia is a prevalent but poorly understood complication of diabetes mellitus. Here, we identify orphan nuclear receptor Nur77 as a critical suppressor of diabetic anemia. Nur77 expression was downregulated in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) from diabetic patients with anemia. In multiple diabetic mouse models, knockout of Nur77 induced anemia, a phenotype recapitulated by bone marrow transplantation. Mechanistically, Nur77 functioned as a transcriptional repressor in HSPCs, whose deficiency, together with diabetes-associated epigenetic modifications, enhanced chromatin accessibility and expression of genes involved in myeloid leukocyte differentiation. Consequently, this led to myeloid leukocyte-biased differentiation of HSPCs at the expense of erythroid lineage. Pharmacological upregulation of Nur77 with its agonist cytosporone B (Csn-B) effectively prevented anemia in diabetic mice. Clinically, Nur77 levels in HSPCs of diabetic patient negatively correlated with anemia occurrence. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel Nur77-mediated pathway in diabetic anemia pathogenesis and propose Nur77 as a new therapeutic target.

43005267.author: Biswas A

43008312.title: Characterizing clinical heterogeneity by whole-genome sequencing of 591 patients with Hemoglobin H disease.
43008312.author: Liu Y
43008312.abstract: Hemoglobin H (Hb H) disease, caused by the functional loss in three of the four α-globin genes, exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity that is not fully explained by primary α-globin genotypes. The genetic modifiers contributing to this phenotypic variability remain incompletely understood. Here, we present the largest whole-genome sequencing (WGS) study of Hb H disease to date, including 591 well-characterized patients and 1,246 ancestry matched controls from Southern China. Case-control GWAS identified two independent variants at the α-globin cluster, rs199594877 and rs34583256, with higher alternative allele frequencies in patients than in controls; rs199594877 was particularly enriched in patients with Hb Constant Spring (HCS). Case-only GWAS across 50 quantitative clinical traits identified six loci associated with hematological and iron metabolism phenotypes. At the HBS1L-MYB (HMIP) locus, rs11759553 was associated with increased Hb Bart's (γ4) levels (P = 3.66 × 10⁻¹⁴). In contrast to its beneficial effects in β-hemoglobinopathies, this association suggests that HMIP variation may have distinct biological consequences in Hb H disease. Together, these findings expand our understanding of the genetic architecture of phenotypic heterogeneity in Hb H disease and establish a comprehensive phenome-genome resource for α-thalassemia, providing candidate loci for further functional and clinical investigation.

43034677.title: Direct oral anticoagulants versus vitamin K antagonists for the treatment of venous thromboembolism in adults with sickle cell disease: a Bayesian meta-analysis.
43034677.author: Le Jeune S
43034677.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used as alternatives to vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) for the treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD). However, comparative evidence is limited to small observational studies, and prior frequentist meta-analyses may be unreliable due to sparse data and zero-event outcomes.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of DOACs versus VKAs for VTE treatment in adults with SCD.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis of studies comparing DOACs with VKAs in patients with SCD and VTE. PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to March 2026. Primary outcomes were recurrent VTE and major bleeding (MB). Bayesian random-effects models with weakly informative priors were used to estimate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Posterior probabilities were derived using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling.
RESULTS: Four retrospective studies including 271 patients (155 DOACs and 116 VKAs) were included. Recurrent VTE did not differ between groups (OR, 0.82; 95% CrI, 0.38-1.75), with a 67.1% posterior probability favoring DOACs, indicating equipoise. DOACs were associated with a significantly lower risk of MB (OR, 0.25; 95% CrI, 0.07-0.80), with a 99.2% probability of superiority. Between-study heterogeneity was low (τ = 0.15 for recurrent VTE; τ = 0.30 for MB).
CONCLUSION: DOACs demonstrate comparable efficacy to VKAs for preventing recurrent VTE in SCD, with a clinically meaningful reduction in MB. Given their safety profile and convenience, DOACs may be preferred; randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

43018999.title: Targeting TMPRSS6 in β-thalassemia: of mice and men.
43018999.author: Finberg KE

43033915.title: Comparison of pegfilgrastim and daily G-CSF for CD34(+) cell mobilization in healthy donors and post-transplant engraftment: The Pegfilgrastim-23 Study.
43033915.author: Hatase M
43033915.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pegfilgrastim (Peg-G), a long-acting formulation of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF), enables single-dose administration and effectively mobilizes CD34+ cells into the peripheral blood of healthy donors undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. However, prospective comparisons with conventional daily G-CSF (Daily-G) regarding mobilization efficacy and safety remain limited. Moreover, no previous studies have compared the differentiation profiles of CD34+ cells mobilized by these two agents.
METHODS: In this multicenter, prospective observational study, we assessed the efficacy, kinetics, safety and differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34+ cells induced by either 7.2 mg dose of Peg-G on day 1 (n = 29) or Daily-G at 400 μg/m2/day from day 1 (n = 31) in 60 healthy related donors scheduled to undergo CD34+ cell collection. Hematopoietic engraftment was also evaluated in 60 recipients following infusion of the collected peripheral blood stem cells.
RESULTS: Of the 60 enrolled donors, 50 were evaluable for peripheral blood CD34+ cell counts. The mean CD34+ cell counts were 85.6 ± 48.0 × 10⁶/L in the Peg-G group and 84.6 ± 42.4 × 10⁶/L in the Daily-G group, with no significant difference between the groups (P = .992). Similar findings were observed in the analyses stratified by collection on days 4 and day 5. No significant differences were observed in the differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34⁺ cells. The kinetics of peripheral blood cell counts were generally comparable between the groups in both the day 4 and day 5 collection cohorts, except for a higher white blood cell count on day 4 in the Peg-G group among donors collected on day 5. In exploratory analyses, CD34⁺ cell mobilization efficacy was not correlated with day 4 serum G-CSF concentrations, donor age, body weight, body mass index, or body surface area in either of the treatment groups. Adverse events were common but predominantly consisted of pain-related symptoms that were manageable with supportive care. Grade 3 adverse events included liver dysfunction in three donors and hypertension in one. All laboratory abnormalities and clinical symptoms resolved by the follow-up assessment, and no grade ≥4 adverse events were observed in any donor. Median times to neutrophil engraftment were 16 and 15 days in the Peg-G and Daily-G groups, respectively (P = .73), and those to platelet engraftment were 30 and 27 days, respectively (P = .68).
CONCLUSIONS: Single-dose 7.2-mg Peg-G and conventional Daily-G resulted in comparable peripheral blood CD34⁺ cell mobilization and differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34⁺ cells in healthy related donors, with generally manageable safety profiles. No significant differences in the time to neutrophil or platelet engraftment were observed between recipients in the two groups. These findings suggest that both mobilization strategies are clinically applicable and that regimen selection may be tailored according to drug-specific characteristics and donor convenience.

43025899.title: Ravulizumab Shows Favorable Survival and Improves Clinical Markers in Children With HSCT-TMA: Results of a Phase 3 Trial.
43025899.author: Locatelli F
43025899.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (HSCT-TMA) is a rare, life-threatening complication that can lead to multiorgan failure and death. The ALXN1210-TMA-314 global, Phase 3, open-label, single-arm trial evaluated ravulizumab, a C5 inhibitor, for treatment of HSCT-TMA in children (NCT04557735). Eligible participants aged ≥ 28 days to < 18 years had HSCT-TMA within 12 months from HSCT, which persisted for ≥ 72 h despite initial management. Participants received weight-based ravulizumab plus best supportive care during the 26-week treatment period, followed by a 26-week follow-up period. The protocol-defined primary endpoint was complete TMA response during the treatment period. Key secondary endpoints included individual TMA response components (proteinuria, platelets, and lactate dehydrogenase/schistocytes), overall survival (OS), and safety. Of 41 enrolled participants (mean age, 7.6 years; 51.2% female), 28 (68.3%) completed treatment, and 24 (58.5%) completed the study. Through the treatment period, 7 (17.1%) participants achieved complete TMA response, and 22 (53.7%) achieved partial TMA response; 29 (70.7%) participants achieved improvement in ≥ 1 TMA response component. Estimated OS was 92.6% at Day 100, 87.2% at Week 26, and 73.4% at Week 52. During treatment, a low incidence of serious TEAEs was assessed by investigators as related to ravulizumab (3 participants, 7.3%); no new safety signals were identified. No meningococcal infections were reported. In this global Phase 3 trial in children with HSCT-TMA, ravulizumab treatment resulted in excellent OS and normalization of early laboratory markers of TMA in many patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT04557735.

43020333.title: Bone marrow niche disruption via interferon gamma-mediated CXCL9/CXCL10 secretion after allogeneic transplantation.
43020333.author: Kimura M
43020333.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a significant complication of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Recent studies have elucidated the susceptibility of the bone marrow (BM) to GVHD, demonstrating a correlation between post-transplant cytopenia and BM niche impairment. However, the mechanisms underlying the damage to perivascular stromal cells, a critical element of the BM niche, remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the effects of alloimmune responses on BM niche populations, identify the mechanism underlying BM niche disruption after allo-HSCT, and highlight the CXCL9/CXCL10-CXCR3 axis as a potential therapeutic target.
STUDY DESIGN: Using murine allogeneic BMT models, we characterized hematopoietic and perivascular niche alterations by flow cytometry, confocal imaging, and single-cell RNA sequencing. The effects of inflammatory cytokines on stromal cells were examined using in vitro co-culture and cytokine-stimulation assays. The role of IFN-γ signaling was further evaluated using IFN-γ receptor-deficient recipients. Spatial interactions between T cells and perivascular niche cells were quantified by confocal imaging, and the functional contribution of CXCL9/CXCL10-CXCR3 signaling was assessed using the selective CXCR3 antagonist AMG487.
RESULTS: This study demonstrated that direct niche cell damage by inflammatory cytokines, such as interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), and inflammatory T cell relocation within the BM owing to excessive CXCL9 and CXCL10 secretion from niche cells, which is induced by IFN-γ signaling, result in further damage to niche cells. Pharmacological blockade of CXCL9/CXCL10 signaling by a selective CXCR3 antagonist mitigated T cell localization close to BM niche cells, with a concomitant reduction in niche cell damage.
CONCLUSION: These findings identify IFN-γ-driven inflammation and CXCL9/CXCL10-CXCR3-mediated T-cell localization as key mechanisms of perivascular niche disruption after allo-BMT. Targeting T-cell-niche interactions may provide a strategy to preserve BM niche integrity and promote hematopoietic recovery after allogeneic transplantation.

43020331.title: Caregiver Stress and Coping during Pediatric Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant: Perspectives of Caregivers and Healthcare Providers.
43020331.author: Olsavsky AL
43020331.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HCT) is potentially curative, it also carries risks and challenges, including lengthy hospitalizations, a risk of life-threatening complications, and demanding medical regimens. Thus, there are high levels of burden and psychological distress among caregivers of children who undergo HCT. However, limited research has explored healthcare provider perspectives on caregivers' pediatric HCT experiences, nor integrated those perspectives with those of caregivers. As healthcare providers partner with caregivers throughout the HCT process, they may be uniquely positioned to identify needs and provide additional support for caregivers during pediatric HCT.
OBJECTIVE(S): The objective of this paper was to explore caregiver and HCT healthcare provider perspectives of caregiver and family experiences across the pediatric HCT process, as identifying areas of agreement and disagreement may inform targeted interventions to support caregiver wellbeing during pediatric HCT.
STUDY DESIGN: This cross-sectional, qualitative pilot study recruited caregivers (n=12) of children 6-24 months post-HCT for individual semi-structured interviews, as well as HCT healthcare providers (i.e., nurses, psychosocial providers, physicians; n=13 in 3 focus groups) from a large freestanding children's hospital in the Midwestern United States. Interviews were coded via inductive qualitative content analysis.
RESULTS: Caregivers and healthcare providers exhibited high agreement regarding caregivers' HCT experiences, which tended to broadly fall into HCT-related stress and coping. Both groups described high levels of caregiver stress; this included causes of stress, such as the child's medical course and balancing competing demands, as well as the expression of heightened emotional distress. Both groups also described caregivers' coping; this included caregiver use of social or relational support, a reliance on private coping, and employing acceptance, adaptive disengagement, and active coping methods. Caregivers and healthcare providers presented some differing foci, with healthcare providers focusing most on symptom-related stress and caregivers emphasizing multiple stressors, including their child's medical course, symptoms, and social isolation.
CONCLUSION(S): There was significant overlap in caregiver and HCT healthcare provider perspectives, as well as areas of divergence, identifying potential opportunities for increased support during care. Findings may inform points of intervention or additional integrated clinical care to ultimately support optimal caregiver and family experiences during pediatric HCT. In particular, additional psychosocial support is needed to mitigate caregiver stress and support caregiver coping during pediatric HCT.

43014546.title: The effect of coping strategies on overall survival and other outcomes after allogeneic stem cell transplant.
43014546.author: Foright RM
43014546.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HCT) carries significant risks with morbidity and mortality rates ranging from 10-30%. The ability to cope with the physical and psychological symptoms of HCT can affect outcomes; however, research on this topic is limited.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to understand how different coping strategies affect clinical outcomes in HCT.
STUDY DESIGN: HCT patients were recruited to this single center, prospective, observational study and completed the Brief-COPE assessment prior to HCT. Brief-COPE is a 28-item questionnaire that measures 14 different coping strategy facets. We evaluated associations between pre-HCT coping strategy and outcomes including overall survival, relapse, non-relapse mortality (NRM), transplant length of stay (LOS), and quality of life (QOL) (PROMIS Global Health) at 1-year post-HCT. Overall survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank tests for group comparisons. Cumulative incidence functions with Gray's test were used for relapse and NRM. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) for overall survival, relapse, and NRM, adjusted for age, conditioning regimen intensity, diagnosis, Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation-specific Comorbidity Index (HCT-CI), and Disease Risk Index (DRI). To assess longitudinal associations between Brief-COPE facets and outcomes, linear mixed-effects models were fitted with random intercepts for patients. Models included time and a facet × time interaction to evaluate changes over time. False Discovery Rate correction was applied to adjust for multiple comparisons. Baseline characteristics were compared using Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables and t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests for continuous variables, as appropriate.
RESULTS: Participants (n=50) ranged from 44-66 years of age and were predominantly white (92%) men (66%). Increased use of the positive reframing coping strategy was associated with increased overall survival (log-rank: p=0.0007), decreased relapse (Gray's: p=0.034), and a trend towards decreased non-relapse mortality (Gray's: p=0.0544). On multivariable analysis, these improvements remained significant for overall survival (HR: 0.36, p=0.027) and relapse (HR: 0.55, p=0.012); additionally, positive reframing was associated with improved QOL (ß=1.14). Acceptance, another coping strategy, was also associated with increased overall survival (log-rank: p=0.0112, multivariate HR: 0.34, p=0.013).
CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the use of positive reframing or acceptance as coping strategies are associated with increased overall survival, decreased relapse, and improved quality of life. Further research is needed to understand whether interventions targeting positive reframing, acceptance, or other adaptive coping strategies could improve clinical outcomes in patients undergoing HCT.

43014544.title: Thiotepa/Busulfan/Cyclophosphamide versus Busulfan/Thiotepa Conditioning For Autologous Stem Cell Transplantation in CNS Lymphoma: A Single-Center Comparative and Descriptive Experience.
43014544.author: Khouderchah C
43014544.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) with thiotepa-based conditioning improves outcomes in primary CNS lymphoma (PCNSL), but standard thiotepa/busulfan/cyclophosphamide (TBC) conditioning is associated with substantial toxicity, particularly among older or less fit patients. Busulfan/thiotepa (BuTT) conditioning reduces busulfan and thiotepa dose intensity in addition to omitting cyclophosphamide, and has been proposed as a better-tolerated alternative, but comparative real-world data remain limited.
OBJECTIVE(S): To compare outcomes of TBC versus BuTT conditioning in patients with PCNSL in first complete remission (CR1) at the time of ASCT; outcomes among patients treated outside this CR1 consolidation setting are described in the Supplement.
STUDY DESIGN: We retrospectively identified all adult patients undergoing ASCT for PCNSL or SCNSL at a single center (January 2010-January 2026). Cohort 1 comprised patients with PCNSL in CR1 who received TBC (n=18) or BuTT (n=18), analyzed comparatively; an additional 37 patients treated outside this CR1 setting are presented descriptively in the Supplement given their heterogeneity.
RESULTS: In Cohort 1, BuTT recipients were significantly older (median 69 vs. 52 years), more often female, and had lower Karnofsky performance status than TBC recipients, consistent with an institutional practice of reserving BuTT for less fit patients since 2020. One- and 2-year overall survival were 94% (TBC) and 100% (BuTT); 1- and 2-year progression-free survival were 89% and 93%, respectively (log-rank p=NS for both). Grade 3-4 mucositis was less frequent with BuTT (28% vs. 72%) despite the expected direction of selection bias, and this difference persisted in a pooled institutional analysis of all patients treated with each regimen (32% vs. 78%, n=73). Both deaths in Cohort 1 were non-relapse mortality in TBC recipients; no BuTT recipients died.
CONCLUSION(S): In this comparison - including, to our knowledge, one of the largest reported BuTT cohorts to date - BuTT conditioning appeared to achieve similar early disease control to TBC in PCNSL patients in CR1 at short follow-up, with lower rates of severe mucositis and no non-relapse mortality, though current data cannot establish statistical equivalence and cannot exclude a late erosion of disease control with reduced-intensity conditioning. Larger, prospective, multi-center studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings and define BuTT's role beyond the CR1 setting.

43008780.title: Endothelial Contributions to Venous Thrombus Resolution.
43008780.author: Hauck M
43008780.abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is an obstructive vascular condition with an incidence of ~1 in 1000 adults per year. Complications of DVT include post-thrombotic syndrome, which is debilitating and painful, and pulmonary embolism, which is life-threatening. Current treatments for DVT are associated with increased risks of bleeding, infection, or re-thrombosis, and fail to accelerate natural venous thrombus resolution. Venous thrombus resolution occurs through a process of organization that involves thrombus retraction away from the vein, fibrinolysis of the thrombus, and the formation of vascular channels within and around the thrombus. Endothelial cell (EC)-lined vascular channels are present in rodent and human resolving thrombi. Rodent models of DVT show that thrombus neovascularization occurs as early as 3-4 days after thrombus induction and increases progressively thereafter throughout thrombus resolution. The extent to which thrombus neovascularization contributes to its resolution, as well as the source of the ECs that vascularize the resolving thrombus, are unclear. Circumstantial evidence suggests that neovascularization is driven by resident ECs that ingress into the resolving thrombus, while circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) promote neovascularization in a paracrine manner. Resident ECs and EPCs also contribute to thrombus fibrinolysis. The aim of this review is to describe the role of ECs and EPCs in DVT resolution, and the potential of promoting thrombus endothelialization and vascularization for the treatment of DVT. We will also outline knowledge gaps in the understanding of EC/EPC-mediated contributions to DVT resolution. The promotion of EC-mediated thrombus resolution represents a novel therapeutic strategy for DVT.

43008313.title: Active Surveillance of JAK2V617F Clonal Hematopoiesis Toward Myeloproliferative Neoplasms.
43008313.author: Loeffler L
43008313.abstract: The aim was to characterize longitudinal JAK2V617F (JAK2) variant allele frequency (VAF) trajectories in individuals without MPN undergoing active surveillance, and to assess whether MPN can be detected at an earlier stage, resulting in lower clonal burden and less bone marrow fibrosis. In the Danish General Suburban Population Study (N=19,958, 2010-2013), we used retrospective measurement of JAK2 on biobanked samples in 2016-2017 and identified 92 JAK2-positive individuals with VAF≥1% that were without MPN at baseline in 2010-2013. Of these, 20 were diagnosed with MPN by clinical referral between 2010-2018. The remaining 72 were reinvited for active MPN surveillance (2018-2026), of whom 61 are included in the present study. Longitudinal JAK2 VAF was quantified using droplet digital PCR, and mixed-effects models were used to estimate clonal growth and blood cell trajectories. Median follow-up to MPN diagnosis was 7.4 years. Referral-diagnosed MPN cases exhibited a relative clonal growth rate of 34.3% per year (p<0.001). Among the 61 undergoing surveillance, 20 were diagnosed with MPN, exhibiting a relative clonal growth rate of 12.7% per year (p=0.003), whereas the remaining 41 did not develop MPN nor showed VAF progression (p=0.628). Within-individual and between-individual variance in VAF was 4.9% and 95.1%, respectively. Platelet counts increased 10.3×10⁹/L/year for surveillance-detected MPN and 44.5×10⁹/L/year for referral-diagnosed MPN. Surveillance-detected MPN had lower VAF at diagnosis (median 13.0% vs 41.3%) and less bone marrow fibrosis (grade 0: 80% vs 15%) than referral-diagnosed MPN. Active surveillance detects MPN with lower clonal burden and less bone marrow fibrosis.

43008795.title: Orelabrutinib plus R-CHOP in patients with newly diagnosed non-GCB double-expressor DLBCL: A single-arm, phase II study.
43008795.author: Yang Y
43008795.abstract: Double-expressor diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DE-DLBCL) patients, defined by co-expression of MYC proto-oncogene protein (≥40%) and B-cell lymphoma 2 protein (≥50%), typically have poor outcomes with the traditional first-line R-CHOP regimen. We conducted a multicentre, single-arm, phase II study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of first-line orelabrutinib plus R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone), designated O-RCHOP, in patients with non-germinal centre B-cell-like (non-GCB) DE-DLBCL. From 19 November 2021 to 6 February 2025, 49 patients were enrolled. With a median follow-up of 26.6 months, median event-free survival (EFS), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were not reached, and the estimated 2-year EFS, PFS and OS rates were 82.0% (95% confidence intervals [CIs]: 71.2%-94.3%), 82.0% (95% CI: 71.2%-94.3%) and 97.9% (95% CI: 94.0%-100.0%) respectively. At the end of treatment, the complete response rate was 89.8% (44/49; 95% CI: 77.8%-96.6%), and the objective response rate was 95.9% (47/49; 95% CI: 86.0%-99.5%). Grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 51.0% of patients, with neutropenia (38.8%) being the most common. No patients died because of AEs. Genetic alteration profiling revealed that the frequently mutated genes were Pim-1 proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase (PIM1; 63.6%), MYD88 innate immune signal transduction adaptor (MYD88; (51.5%) and CD79b molecule (CD79B; 48.5%). O-RCHOP achieved encouraging efficacy with a manageable safety profile in newly diagnosed DE-DLBCL, supporting its feasibility as a first-line regimen.

43008305.title: Racial and Ethnic Differences in the Incidence of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis Across the Age Spectrum.
43008305.author: Velazquez J
43008305.abstract: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is an inflammatory myeloid neoplasia with an annual incidence of 5 cases per million children <15 and 1-2 cases per million adults ≥18. Pediatric LCH incidence is known to vary by race/ethnicity; less is known among adults. Therefore, we sought to compare LCH incidence by race/ethnicity in the United States (US) across the age spectrum using data from the US Cancer Statistics (USCS) database. LCH incidence data (2010-2022) were obtained from the USCS database and stratified by age at diagnosis and race/ethnicity. Age was defined as childhood (0-14 years), adolescent/young adult (AYA; 15-39 years), and adult (40+ years); race/ethnicity as non-Hispanic White (NHW), non-Hispanic Black, non-Hispanic Asian/Pacific Islander, non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native, and Hispanic. Age-adjusted incidence rate-ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using SEER*Stat. A total of 4,080 childhood, 1,399 AYA, and 1,819 adult incident cases with LCH were identified in the USCS database. Hispanic children experienced significantly higher LCH IRRs compared to NHW children (IRRHispanic_children_0to14=1.16, 95% CI: 1.08-1.24), while Hispanic AYAs and adults exhibited significantly lower IRRs compared to NHWs AYAs and adults (IRRHispanic_AYAs_15to39=0.74, 95% CI: 0.64-0.85; IRRHispanic_adults_40+=0.54, 95% CI: 0.45-0.65). A sub-analysis among childhood cases demonstrated the strongest effects were among Hispanic children aged 1-4 and 5-9 compared to NHW children (IRRHispanic_children_1to4=1.35, 95% CI: 1.20-1.51; IRRHispanic_children_5to9=1.16, 95% CI: 1.01-1.33). Hispanic children, particularly those 1-9 years, experience the highest incidence of LCH; a trend not observed in Hispanic AYAs and adults. These findings suggest differences in LCH etiology across the age spectrum.

43003201.title: Platelet NLRP3 signaling promotes thromboinflammation and organ injury in sepsis.
43003201.author: Dai Y
43003201.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is characterized by dysregulated host responses to infection, leading to microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction, and death. Although NLRP3 regulates platelet activation and arterial thrombosis, its role in sepsis-associated thromboinflammation remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the contribution of platelet NLRP3 to microvascular thrombosis, inflammation, and organ injury during sepsis.
RESULTS: Pulmonary IL-1β increased during sepsis and colocalized with platelets. Platelet NLRP3 deficiency attenuated pulmonary IL-1β elevation, whereas adoptive transfer of wild-type, but not NLRP3-deficient, platelets increased pulmonary IL-1β in NLRP3-deficient recipients. Platelet NLRP3 deficiency improved survival, reduced pulmonary and hepatic microvascular thrombosis, and attenuated organ injury. Furthermore, NLRP3 deficiency reduced platelet activation, phosphatidylserine exposure, platelet-neutrophil interactions, inflammatory cell accumulation, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, and inflammatory cytokine levels. Importantly, reduced platelet activation, phosphatidylserine exposure, and platelet-neutrophil interactions were evident at 6 hours after cecal ligation and puncture, before detectable differences in bacterial burden. Septic plasma induced platelet NLRP3 activation and IL-1β maturation through TLR4/MyD88-sensitive signaling. IL-1β neutralization attenuated septic plasma-induced platelet activation, phosphatidylserine exposure, and platelet-neutrophil interactions, whereas recombinant IL-1β restored these responses in NLRP3-deficient platelets.
CONCLUSIONS: Platelet NLRP3 contributes to pulmonary IL-1β responses and promotes thromboinflammation during experimental sepsis. Its deficiency reduces microvascular thrombosis and organ injury while improving survival, suggesting platelet NLRP3 as a potential therapeutic target.

43001447.title: Phagocytosis activity is retained by JMML macrophages and increased by CD47 inhibition.
43001447.author: Wang J
43001447.abstract: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia (JMML) is a childhood myeloid malignancy driven by RAS (rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog) pathway mutations, characterized by myeloid cell accumulation and organ infiltration. We investigated how clonal macrophage polarization, phagocytic function and CD47 (cluster of differentiation 47) expression contribute to immune dysregulation. Human PTPN11 (protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type 11) -mutated JMML spleens exhibited higher M1-like macrophage levels than KRAS (KRAS proto-oncogene, GTPase)-mutated cases or controls. Both human JMML macrophages and murine cells from Mx-Cre;Ptpn11D61Y/+ mice retained phagocytic activity, with M1-like cells being the most active. CD47, a 'don't eat me' signal, was upregulated in human and murine JMML cells; its blockade enhanced in vitro phagocytosis. In a patient-derived xenograft model, the CD47 inhibitor magrolimab reduced leukaemia burden in the spleen but not the bone marrow. No synergy was observed between magrolimab and azacitidine. These findings demonstrate that clonal JMML macrophages retain phagocytic activity and contribute to an inflammatory phenotype. While CD47 blockade shows limited therapeutic potential, this study clarifies the interplay between macrophage polarization, immune evasion and inflammation, providing a basis for future JMML strategies.

43008779.title: Pantothenate Metabolic Alterations in PROS1 Mutation Carriers and the Antithrombotic Effects of Pantethine.
43008779.author: Xia M
43008779.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1-mutation patients through integrated multi-omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models.
METHODS: Serum metabolomics, siRNA-mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE-2 cells, murine thrombosis models, and endothelial cell functional assays were employed.
RESULTS: Patients with PROS1 mutations exhibited significantly reduced serum levels of pantothenate derivatives, particularly pantetheine. siRNA-mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE-2 cells recapitulated this metabolic disturbance. In vivo, pantethine supplementation attenuated thrombus formation and platelet activation in murine models, accompanied by reduced serum levels of vWF and ICAM-1, and increased TFPI. In vitro, pantethine pretreatment suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation and reduced endothelial reactive oxygen species, counteracting IL-1β-induced procoagulant phenotype, leading to downregulation of vWF and ICAM-1 and upregulation of TFPI and THBD. Furthermore, pantethine-conditioned endothelial cells reduced responsiveness of co-incubated platelets, including attenuated spreading, aggregation, and activation. These findings associate PROS1 mutation-driven metabolic alterations with thrombotic risk, and suggest a metabolic-endothelial-platelet mode of interaction.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that patients with PROS1 mutations exhibit reduced circulating pantothenate derivatives, and that pantethine attenuates murine thrombosis and modulates endothelial and platelet function in vitro. These findings identify a metabolic-endothelial-platelet association in protein S deficiency. Whether PROS1 mutations directly cause pantothenate metabolic disturbance, and whether this disturbance mediates thrombosis, require testing in PROS1-deficient in vivo models.
