43003889.title: Cryopreservation of academic CAR T-cell products: methodological recommendations from the EBMT practice harmonisation and guidelines committee.
43003889.author: Bonig H
43003889.abstract: Academic CAR T-cell manufacturing is rapidly expanding across Europe, but cryopreservation practices remain heterogeneous, raising concerns about product comparability. While cryopreservation is essential for later infusion, storage of surplus cells, or treatment postponement, no specific harmonized guidelines exist for CAR T-cell products. An EBMT survey (52 academic centers) revealed wide variability in freezing timing, cryomedium composition, device choice, storage temperatures, and post-thaw quality control. To address these gaps, EBMT organized a workshop using its harmonisation methodology. A panel of experts reviewed survey data, literature, and professional experience to draft consensus recommendations. Key recommendations include: performing cryopreservation as soon as possible after manufacturing (preferably ≤48 h), initiating freezing within 30 min of cryomedium addition, and using controlled-rate freezing to at least -80 °C, with long-term storage below -120 °C whenever feasible. Retention samples, post-thaw viability, identity testing, and validated transportation procedures are considered mandatory. Liquid nitrogen and Peltier-based controlled-rate freezing systems were regarded as technically equivalent, while -80 °C passive freezing has been used successfully and may serve as a back-up method, local confirmation of suitability in a formal method validation provided. These consensus-based recommendations seek to establish technical recommendations for CAR-T cryopreservation for groups currently establishing academic manufacturing of CAR-T products.

43020329.title: Attrition Factors in Patients with Metastatic Melanoma Screened for Tumor Infiltrating Lymphocyte Therapy.
43020329.author: Pachori A
43020329.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following recent regulatory approval, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy has entered the treatment landscape for advanced melanoma, but its delivery requires coordinated multidisciplinary care, including surgical tumor procurement (TIL harvest), cellular manufacturing, lymphodepleting chemotherapy, and high-dose interleukin-2. Real-world attrition across this pathway remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of 59 patients with anti-programmed death 1-refractory metastatic melanoma referred for TIL therapy. Patients were categorized into 4 cohorts: eligible, underwent TIL harvest, and received TIL infusion (cohort A); eligible, underwent TIL harvest, but did not receive infusion (cohort B); eligible, but did not undergo TIL harvest (cohort C); and ineligible (cohort D). We evaluated attrition factors, exploratory predictors of pathway completion, and clinical outcomes among treated patients.
RESULTS: Of 59 referred patients, 25 (42.4%) were in cohort A, 9 (15.3%) in cohort B, 17 (28.8%) in cohort C, and 8 (13.6%) in cohort D. The most common reasons for attrition were rapid disease progression and decline in performance status, occurring both before procurement and after TIL harvest but before infusion. The out-of-specification product rate was 14.7% (5/34 patients who underwent procurement); 2 of these 5 patients did not receive infusion. No baseline factor, including M substage, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), number of prior treatment lines, treatment immediately before evaluation, or liver or brain metastases, was significantly associated with undergoing TIL harvest. Elevated LDH at TIL evaluation was significantly associated with higher odds of not receiving infusion after procurement (odds ratio, 12.0; 95% CI, 1.22-117.8; P=0.02). Among treated patients, median time from evaluation to TIL harvest was 41 days and from TIL harvest to infusion was 50 days. Among 22 response-evaluable patients, the overall response rate was 40.9%, disease control rate was 59.1%, median progression-free survival was 2.27 months, and median overall survival was 6.11 months.
CONCLUSION: Real-world attrition during TIL therapy was substantial and was driven predominantly by clinical deterioration rather than manufacturing failure alone. These findings support earlier referral, streamlined care pathways, and refined patient selection to improve successful TIL delivery in advanced melanoma.

43014348.title: Clinical phenotypes, autoimmunity and outcomes in Rosai-Dorfman disease: An international multicentre cohort study.
43014348.author: Sen M
43014348.abstract: Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare histiocytic neoplasm with diverse clinical behaviour and immune abnormalities with unknown clinical significance. We performed a retrospective cohort study of 162 patients with RDD from 2003 to 2025 at five international referral centres. Median age was 48 years and 64.8% were female. Multisystem disease occurred in 87 patients (53.7%), commonly involving skin/subcutaneous tissue (49.4%), lymph nodes (39.5%) and bones (34%). Molecular testing was available for 102 patients; 40 (39.2%) were mitogen-activated protein kinase/rat sarcoma virus oncogene homolog signaling pathway (MAPK/RAS)-altered, commonly with kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS) or mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAP2K/MEK) alterations. MAPK/RAS alterations were associated with multisystem disease (p = 0.0034). Autoimmune disease (AID) was documented in 29 patients (17.9%), usually preceding RDD, and 45/95 patients (47.4%) with available autoantibody status had at least one positive autoantibody. Among 153 patients with response data, objective response occurred in 94 (61.4%). Response distribution differed by disease extent; single-system disease was associated with more complete responses and less progression than multisystem disease. At a median follow-up of 2.49 years, eight deaths occurred; 5-year overall survival was 93.4%. AID and autoantibody positivity were not associated with response or overall survival. These findings support disease extent and molecular status as clinically relevant dimensions of RDD assessment, while autoimmune and serological abnormalities should be interpreted in clinical context.
